reason: Step to the interface designing after DB schema generation

scenario.draft: Validate that a customer can retrieve all comments for a given post, including both public comments and their own private comments. Begin by creating a customer and a post, then add several comments (public and private) by different users including the requesting customer. Confirm that only public comments and the customer's own private comments are returned, and that other users' private comments are not included in the list.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to which comments will be attached.
Add a variety of comments (public/private, different authors) to the post for realistic testing.

scenario.draft: Test the error response when retrieving comments for a non-existent postId. Attempt to list comments using an invalid or random postId and verify a 404 or meaningful error response indicating the post does not exist.

Ensure that only authorized users can retrieve comment lists. Attempt to access the comments as an unauthorized or anonymous user and confirm access is denied with a proper authentication or permission error.

Test successful retrieval of a customer's full details by their unique customerId as an administrator. Precondition: Ensure that a customer account exists via the customer creation endpoint and capture the generated customerId. As an administrator, request the full details of this customer and expect to receive all defined fields (id, email, phone, status, audit fields) matching the prior creation data.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer to obtain a valid customerId for detailed retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test error scenario: attempt to retrieve a customer detail record using a non-existent or invalid customerId as an administrator. Expect a 404 not found error and that no sensitive data is leaked. This ensures the API correctly validates that the customer exists and handles error cases gracefully.

Test successful registration of a customer using valid, unique email and phone values. Submit a complete payload per IAimallBackendCustomer.ICreate, confirm all response fields match input values and audit fields (id, timestamps) are properly assigned. Expect sensitive fields such as password_hash returned according to business logic. This validates the customer registration workflow.

Test failure when trying to register a customer using an email that already exists in the system. First, create a customer with a specific email, then attempt to register a new customer with the same email, expecting a conflict or validation error for email uniqueness. Business logic must strictly enforce this constraint.

dependencies.purpose: Register the initial customer to establish a unique email constraint for this test.

scenario.draft: Test input validation: try to create a customer using an invalid email format and verify the request is rejected with a validation error. No new customer should be created. This validates frontend/backend input control.

Test required fields validation: attempt to create a customer but omit a required field such as email or phone. Ensure the API responds with a validation error, and no customer is created. This checks the API's required field enforcement for the registration workflow.

Test successfully updating a customer's information as an administrator. Precondition: Register a new customer and obtain customerId, then submit an update to mutable fields such as phone or status. Verify response reflects updated values and audit fields (updated_at) are changed accordingly. Ensure immutable fields (like id) are not altered.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer to obtain a customerId for update testing.

scenario.draft: Test attempting to update a customer with a new email that is already assigned to another customer. Expect a uniqueness constraint violation error from the API. This scenario ensures enforcement of unique email addresses during updates.

dependencies.purpose: Register the first customer to establish their email address.
Register a second customer whose email will be used for conflict in the update.

scenario.draft: Test updating a non-existent customer by using an invalid or missing customerId. The operation should return a 404 error and not affect any records. This scenario validates not-found error handling for updates.

Test successful hard-delete of a customer account by administrator. Precondition: Register a new customer, then delete using their customerId. Confirm the customer no longer exists by attempting to retrieve details or list customers and expect no result for the deleted account.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer so there is a deletable account for the delete test.

scenario.draft: Test deleting a non-existent customer by passing an invalid or previously deleted customerId. The API must return a 404 error and ensure that no unrelated records are affected. This scenario validates proper error handling and protects data integrity on deletion.

Test successful retrieval of external accounts linked to a valid customer account. Precondition: Create a customer, link at least one external account (such as Google or Apple) using the relevant endpoint, then fetch external accounts to verify all linked accounts are returned with correct data. Ensure only accounts belonging to the customer are visible.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer to obtain their customerId for external account linking.
Link an external account to the test customer before listing.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving external accounts for a customer that has no accounts linked. Expect the API to return an empty list, and ensure this is not treated as an error scenario. This validates correct handling of unlinked accounts in the UX.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer with no external accounts linked, for the retrieval test.

scenario.draft: Test error scenario: attempt to fetch external accounts for an invalid or non-existent customerId as a customer. The response should be a 404 or access denied, with no information returned about any accounts. This ensures robustness and privacy of cross-customer requests.

A seller attempts to update their own profile data, such as changing their business name, email, or contact phone number. Begin by registering a new seller and extracting the sellerId for use in the update operation. Use valid update data for allowed fields. Verify the operation succeeds, the fields are updated, and the audit trail is correct.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new seller and extract sellerId to perform update by the seller.

scenario.draft: A seller tries to update their email to one that already exists for another seller, violating the unique email constraint. First, create two sellers. Attempt to update the second seller’s email to match the first seller’s email. Expect the operation to fail with a uniqueness constraint violation error.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first seller whose email will later be used to test for duplication.
Create the second seller whose account will attempt the duplicate email update.

scenario.draft: A seller attempts to update the profile of another seller (not their own account). After creating two sellers, attempt to update the second seller's profile using the first seller's authentication. The action should be forbidden, returning an authorization error, ensuring sellers can only update their own accounts unless administrator rights are present.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first seller; this account will attempt to update another seller’s profile.
Create the second seller for the ownership test.

scenario.draft: An administrator performs an update on a seller’s information, such as changing the business name or status. Register a seller with standard data; then, as an admin, update the seller’s details. Confirm the update is successful and the data persists correctly.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller who will be updated by the administrator.

scenario.draft: An administrator attempts to update a seller’s information with invalid data (for example, email in incorrect format or missing required fields). After creating a seller, as an admin, attempt updates that violate schema validation. The update should be rejected with meaningful error details for the violation (e.g., format error, missing required fields).

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller who will be updated with invalid data by admin.

scenario.draft: An administrator tries to update a seller by specifying a nonexistent sellerId. Use a random UUID that does not correspond to an existing seller record. The API must return a not found error, with no changes applied in the data layer.

An administrator deletes a seller’s account by sellerId. Create a new seller, then as admin, delete that seller. Attempt to retrieve the seller after deletion to verify that the account has been fully removed with no soft-delete present. The retrieval should return not found; deletion is irreversible.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller account to be deleted in this scenario.
Verify that the seller account is gone after deletion.

scenario.draft: An administrator attempts to delete a seller using a sellerId that does not correspond to any record in the system. Use a random UUID guaranteed not to exist. The API must respond with a not found error and log the incident.

An authenticated administrator retrieves the full list of administrator accounts. The test checks that the API returns all active and suspended administrators, and correctly omits any sensitive authentication data (such as passwords). Only users with proper admin permissions can access this list; any non-admin attempt triggers an authorization error. At least one admin should exist prior to this test; if not, first create an admin account.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure at least one administrator account exists for a realistic list result.

scenario.draft: A non-administrator attempts to retrieve the administrator accounts list. Attempt the GET as a user without administrator privileges and verify access is denied with an appropriate forbidden response.

An administrator searches for administrator accounts filtering by status (e.g., active, suspended, pending) using the advanced search endpoint. Begin by creating several administrators with different statuses. Issue a search for a specific status and confirm the returned results match only accounts with that status, including correct pagination metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Create one or more admin accounts with varying statuses for search filter scenarios.

scenario.draft: An administrator performs a search for administrator accounts using a partial match on the email field. Ensure multiple admins exist with varied emails; submit a search query filtering by a substring of an admin's email. Confirm that the results only include admins whose emails contain the search string.

dependencies.purpose: Create administrator accounts with distinct email patterns for the partial match test.

scenario.draft: An administrator queries the search endpoint with filters or combinations that match no currently registered administrator accounts (e.g., impossible status or random email). Verify the endpoint returns an empty result set with correct pagination information and zero total count.

Verify that all available and active products can be retrieved by the public via GET /aimall-backend/products. Confirm that the endpoint returns a paginated list with proper summary/detail fields as per catalog schema. Execute without authentication and validate that only non-deleted and published products are included in the results.

Test that the endpoint does not return products that are unpublished, marked inactive, or deleted. First, create two products: one active/published and one inactive/deleted using seller/admin API. Retrieve all products and confirm only the active product is present in the list.

dependencies.purpose: Create an active/published product to ensure there is at least one product to list.
Create a product with inactive status or mark as deleted to confirm it's not in the product list.

scenario.draft: Test the pagination mechanism by creating more products than the default page size and verify multiple pages are returned. Also, assess system performance by retrieving pages beyond the result set and confirm proper 'empty' page handling.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple product records to exceed default page size for pagination validation.

scenario.draft: Verify that products can be searched and filtered based on keyword and category by using the PATCH endpoint with appropriate search criteria. Confirm that results only include products matching the search keyword in title/description and filter by selected category ID. Check paginated response and data integrity.

dependencies.purpose: Create products with distinguishable titles/descriptions and specific categories to enable keyword/category search testing.

scenario.draft: Test failure scenario by providing invalid/malformed search criteria (e.g., non-existent category ID, invalid pagination parameters) to the PATCH endpoint. Confirm API returns appropriate error status and message without exposing sensitive data or internal details.

Confirm that advanced search can filter products by their status and by seller_id. First, create products with various statuses (active/inactive) and from multiple sellers, then filter by status and/or seller ID and verify expected results are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create products with different statuses and seller associations to validate filtering logic.

scenario.draft: Ensure full product details can be retrieved by specifying a valid productId. First, create a product and then fetch its details by ID; check that all public and normalized fields are present and match what was inserted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new product to generate a valid productId for subsequent retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test error handling by requesting details for a non-existent or deleted productId. Confirm the system returns a 404 or appropriate error indicating product not found, without leaking system internals.

Check that attempting to access the detail view of a deleted or inactive product does not disclose any product data. Attempt to fetch details for a product that has been 'deleted' to validate business logic and data privacy.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product.
Delete the product by productId before attempting to retrieve details.

scenario.draft: Validate that an authenticated seller can successfully create a new product by supplying all required fields. Confirm that the response contains the fully populated product entity, and verify data persistence by listing or retrieving the product afterward.

Attempt to create a product with invalid or non-existent foreign key values (categoryId, sellerId). Check that the API rejects the request and returns a clear validation error regarding relationship integrity.

Ensure that creating a product with a duplicate title for the same seller is disallowed by business logic. Attempt to create two products under the same seller with identical titles and expect a uniqueness constraint error.

dependencies.purpose: Create initial product with a given title for uniqueness test.

scenario.draft: Check that an administrator can create new products for any seller in the marketplace, including setting advanced properties and overriding defaults. Confirm the response entity and created product persistence.
Attempt product creation with required fields missing (e.g., no title or category). Verify the API returns a validation error for incomplete input and does not create any product record.
Test admin-side enforcement of uniqueness constraints by attempting to create a product with data (e.g., title) that already exists for a seller. Ensure system returns a conflict/validation error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product with a specific seller and title to set up a conflict scenario.

scenario.draft: Test successful advanced search and filtering of RBAC permission definitions by administrator with various filter criteria. The administrator requests permissions with a specific code, partial match in display name, or within certain audit date ranges. The response is verified for correct filtering, pagination, and presence of only authorized data fields. Edge cases such as zero results are included. Error cases involve invalid search parameters or unauthorized access attempts.

dependencies.purpose: Create required test RBAC permission/role definitions to set up search/filter scenarios. This ensures there is known data to be found or excluded according to test filters.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a single RBAC permission role definition by its valid ID as an administrator. First, a permission role is created, and then its unique identifier is used to request full detail. The response is checked for inclusion of all schema fields (code, display_name, description) and appropriate error handling for permission denied or record not found (wrong ID or deleted entry).

dependencies.purpose: Create a permission/role definition to have a valid permissionId for the query.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving RBAC permission detail with an invalid or non-existent permissionId as an administrator. Attempt to fetch a permission by a UUID that does not exist and verify the API returns 404 not found or an appropriate error. Ensure that no sensitive data is exposed on failure.

Test the creation of a new RBAC permission or role definition by submitting valid, required fields (unique code, display_name, description) as an administrator. Verify the response contains the fully populated new resource, and uniqueness constraints on code are enforced. Successful audit logging should be noted.

Test attempting to create a new RBAC permission or role with a code that already exists in the system. The system should reject the request due to uniqueness violation and return a conflict or validation error. Steps involve creating an initial role and then attempting a second creation with the same code.

dependencies.purpose: Create a RBAC permission/role definition with a unique code to later provoke duplication.

scenario.draft: Test updating display_name and description fields for an existing RBAC permission as an administrator. After creating a permission role, submit valid field updates and check that the API returns the updated resource reflecting the changes. Ensure audit logging and that code uniqueness is still enforced if code is being modified.

dependencies.purpose: Create the permission/role definition to be updated.

scenario.draft: Test updating a permission/role's code to a value that collides with an existing role's code, to validate that uniqueness constraint violations are handled correctly with an appropriate error response. Ensure precondition by having at least two roles.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first RBAC permission with a unique code.
Create a second RBAC permission with another code to provoke collision during update.

scenario.draft: Test successful hard deletion of an existing RBAC permission/role definition by ID as an administrator. Create a role and then delete it by its id, confirming the role is fully removed and access afterwards returns 404. Ensure deletion is logged for audit purposes.

dependencies.purpose: Create the permission/role to be deleted for setup of the test.

scenario.draft: Test deleting a RBAC permission/role with a non-existent ID as an administrator. Confirm the API returns not found error and does not inadvertently affect real records. No dependency on actual data setup necessary for this negative scenario.

Test advanced search of a customer's addresses by filtering on recipient_name criteria. First, register a customer account and add multiple addresses for the customer with varying recipient names and cities. Then, perform an address search with a recipient_name substring that matches one of the addresses. Verify that only addresses containing the matching recipient_name are returned in the paginated, filtered list. Confirm that the pagination and sorting work as expected when multiple matches are found.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer account to obtain a valid customerId for address management.
Add multiple address records with different recipient names and cities for the registered customer so the filter has varied data to test against.

scenario.draft: Test the error scenario where an advanced address search is attempted for a nonexistent customerId. Attempt to perform a PATCH search on /customer/customers/{customerId}/addresses using a UUID that does not correspond to any valid customer. Confirm that the system returns an appropriate error (such as 404) indicating the specified customer does not exist, and that no results are returned.

Test advanced search with pagination parameters that exceed the total number of address records for the customer. First, create a customer and add a single address to their account. Then, perform a search with pagination parameters (e.g., page number or offset) that are out of bounds with the available data. The system should respond with an empty array for results, and the pagination metadata should accurately reflect no data for that page.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer to use in the test.
Add an address to the created customer so a single address is available to test pagination.

scenario.draft: Test advanced address search as an administrator, filtering addresses for a customer by the is_default flag. First, create a customer and register several addresses for them, ensuring that at least one address is marked as is_default=true. As an administrator, perform a PATCH search using the is_default filter. Verify that only the address marked as default appears in the search results. Ensure proper permission handling so only admins can query other customers' data.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer and obtain their customerId for address management.
Add multiple addresses for the customer, marking one as is_default=true.

scenario.draft: Test administrator search for a customer's addresses with pagination values that result in an empty page. Register a customer, add a few addresses, then attempt to search addresses with page/offset parameters set beyond the available data. Validate that the response returns an empty data set and correct pagination information (e.g., no further pages).

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer.
Add multiple addresses for the new customer.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a specific address's details for an existing customer. Register a customer and add at least one address. Retrieve the created address using its addressId and the customerId. Verify that all fields match the originally provided data and that the response contains complete, accurate address information.

dependencies.purpose: Create a customer whose address will be tested.
Add an address to the customer, capture the addressId for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test the API response when attempting to retrieve the details of an address using a nonexistent addressId for a valid customer. The system should return an appropriate not-found error, indicating the address does not exist for the specified customer.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test customer to use their customerId.

scenario.draft: Test administrator retrieval of a specific customer address by addressId. As an admin, create a customer and register one or more addresses. Retrieve one address via its addressId and the customer's ID, and check that all fields (address lines, recipient name, etc.) are accurately returned. Confirm no sensitive data is omitted from the admin's perspective.

dependencies.purpose: Create a sample customer for testing.
Add an address as admin to the customer, retrieve the addressId.

scenario.draft: Test the administrator experience when attempting to fetch details for a non-existent addressId for a given customerId. Confirm that an appropriate error (such as 404 not found) is returned and that no sensitive data from unrelated addresses is exposed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a sample customer to use for invalid address lookup.

scenario.draft: Test the creation of a new delivery address for a customer and verify that addresses are correctly associated, with uniqueness constraints enforced for is_default. Register a customer, create multiple addresses setting different is_default flags, and validate that only one address per customer can be set as default through business constraints. Confirm that the response contains correct address details and address linkage to the customer.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer for address management.

scenario.draft: Test that when creating a new address for a customer with an invalid payload (e.g., missing required fields such as address line or recipient name), the API returns a validation error. Register a customer and attempt to create an address omitting mandatory fields or supplying malformed data. Ensure the response is a validation failure with appropriate error messaging.

dependencies.purpose: Register a valid customer for which an invalid address creation will be attempted.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a new configuration entry with all required fields and valid data. First, ensure that the referenced channel and/or section exist if specified. Attempt configuration creation using a new (key, channel_id, section_id) combination and valid value. Expect the operation to return the fully created configuration entity with correct audit timestamps and persisted data.

Test failure when creating a configuration where the (key, channel_id, section_id) combination is already in use. First, create a configuration entry using a specific key along with optional channel and section references. Then, attempt to create another configuration with the same (key, channel_id, section_id). Expect an error indicating uniqueness constraint violation and that the second configuration is not created.

dependencies.purpose: First create a configuration to establish the (key, channel_id, section_id) combination in use; the duplicate creation attempt will then fail as a negative test.

scenario.draft: Test failure if any required fields are missing from the configuration creation request. Attempt to create a configuration omitting one or more required fields (e.g., missing key or value). Expect a validation error response and confirmation that no configuration is created.

Test successful update of a configuration entity's mutable fields (such as key, value, channel_id, or section_id) using a valid configurationId. Perform configuration creation first, then update allowed fields. Expect the updated configuration to reflect changes and updated audit timestamp.

dependencies.purpose: Create a configuration to get a valid configurationId for the update test.

scenario.draft: Test failure case when updating a configuration to a (key, channel_id, section_id) combination that already exists in another configuration. Create two configurations first with unique keys. Attempt to update the second one, setting its (key, channel_id, section_id) to duplicate the first. Expect a uniqueness violation error and the update rejected.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first configuration with a unique key/scope.
Create a second configuration with a different key/scope for later update conflict.

scenario.draft: Test that updating a configuration with a non-existent or invalid configurationId returns an appropriate error (such as 404 Not Found). Attempt to update using a non-existent UUID. Expect the system to return an error and the original configuration to remain unchanged.

Test successful permanent deletion of an existing configuration. Create a configuration first, then delete it using its configurationId. Confirm that the configuration is no longer retrievable and that the API returns no content as the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a configuration in order to have a valid configurationId for deletion.

scenario.draft: Test that attempting to delete a configuration with a non-existent or already deleted configurationId yields a 404 Not Found error. Attempt deletion with an invalid or already removed UUID and confirm the appropriate error response is returned.

Test retrieval of a customer account summary list when at least one customer exists. Register a new customer through the customer creation API, then access the administrator customer listing endpoint. Verify that the new customer is present in the returned list and that all fields match the summary schema.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new customer to ensure at least one account is present for listing.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of the customer account summary list when no customer records exist in the database. Ensure the system is in a clean state with no customers created (e.g., newly provisioned environment). Call the listing endpoint and expect an empty result set or an appropriate empty data structure.

Test searching and paginating customer accounts using the email field as a filter. Register multiple customers with unique emails. Use the advanced search endpoint to look up a customer by a specific email. Confirm that the result contains only the matching customer and that pagination and metadata are accurate.

dependencies.purpose: Register multiple customers with different emails to populate the dataset.

scenario.draft: Test searching for customer accounts using filter criteria that match no customer (e.g., a non-existent email or out-of-range creation date). Confirm the API returns an empty data array and valid pagination metadata indicating zero results.

Test advanced filtering by a combination of account status and creation date range for customer accounts. Create customers with different statuses on different dates, then use the search endpoint to filter for a specific status and date range. Verify that only matching accounts appear in results and pagination is handled correctly.

dependencies.purpose: Register customers with various status values and creation dates for filter combination testing.

scenario.draft: Test updating an existing section under a channel with all valid and mutable fields. As an administrator, create a channel, then create a section under that channel. Use the section and channel IDs to perform an update (e.g., change name, code, display order, or enabled flag) and expect the endpoint to return an updated section entity reflecting the new values. Confirm that only permitted fields are mutable and that audit logging occurs per requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a new channel so that a section can be created and updated under it.
Create a section under the provisioned channel to enable the update operation.

scenario.draft: Test failure when updating a section's code to a value that already exists on a sibling section within the same channel. This ensures the unique constraint on (channel_id, code) is enforced. After creating a channel and two distinct sections, attempt to update the second section's code to that of the first. Confirm the API rejects the update with a conflict error and the section's data is not changed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel as parent context for the test.
Create two sections with different codes under the created channel.

scenario.draft: Test error responses when attempting to update a section using invalid channelId or sectionId (e.g., malformed UUID or non-existent record). Confirm 404 errors and proper error messaging for both cases. This checks input validation and referential integrity enforcement.

Test the soft deletion process for a section under a channel by an administrator. First, create a channel and at least one section within it. Use the channel and section IDs to perform a DELETE. Verify that the section's deleted_at timestamp is set (soft delete) and that it no longer appears in active section listings, but is retained for audit purposes.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a channel for section management.
Create a section under the new channel to be deleted.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a section with a valid channelId but a non-existent or already-deleted sectionId. Verify that a 404 error is returned, and the operation is audit logged.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a channel for the non-existent section deletion test.

scenario.draft: Test that an administrator can retrieve the complete list of system configurations. Ensure that the endpoint returns all configuration entities in accordance with the schema, including global, channel-scoped, and section-scoped configurations. Confirm that the response does not leak sensitive information and includes required audit fields. Use this operation to verify audit consistency and completeness.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one configuration to guarantee predictable non-empty results.

scenario.draft: Test the ability to search system configurations as an administrator using filter criteria and pagination. First, create multiple configuration records with varying values and scopes (global, channel, section). Use the PATCH search endpoint with filters such as key, value, channel_id, and date ranges. Confirm that only configurations matching the criteria are returned and pagination metadata is correct.

dependencies.purpose: Insert multiple configuration entries with diverse properties for filter testing.

scenario.draft: Test the case where the search criteria produce no result (e.g., using an impossible key or date). Confirm that the API returns an empty data array while still providing pagination information.

Test retrieval of a specific configuration entity by its ID as an administrator. First, create a configuration entry, then use its ID to request detail. Confirm that all normalized fields, including key, value, channel_id, and timestamps, are present and accurate in the response. This scenario validates both access control and entity integrity.

dependencies.purpose: Create a sample configuration entity to fetch in detail by its ID.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when requesting a configuration that does not exist (invalid or deleted configurationId). Ensure that the system responds with a 404 error and clear messaging, without leaking any data.

Test successful retrieval of a single administrator's complete profile using a valid, existing UUID and appropriate permissions. This validates that all normalized fields are returned (email, display name, status, permission assignment, timestamps) and no sensitive authentication data is leaked. Scenario involves authenticating as an administrator user, then fetching details for another administrator account already present in the system.

dependencies.purpose: Create an administrator account to ensure a valid UUID exists for retrieval and that permission assignments are correctly set up. Must occur before attempting retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when attempting to retrieve an administrator account using an invalid or non-existent administratorId (malformed UUID or one not present in the system). Expects a proper 404 or validation error response, validating that no data leakage occurs and the error message is clear.

Attempt to retrieve administrator details using insufficient permissions (e.g., as a non-administrator user or customer role). Checks that access is denied and an appropriate error is returned, in line with platform security requirements.

Test successful creation of a new administrator account using valid, complete data. Ensures that required fields (permission_id, email, display name, status) are supplied, user is created, and returned resource includes all fields. Validate that only authorized actors (super admin or permission manager) can perform this operation. Also confirm audit log registration for compliance.

Attempt to create a new administrator using an email that already exists in the system. Should result in a constraint violation and a descriptive error response. Verifies enforcement of unique email per administrator.

dependencies.purpose: Creates the initial administrator with the email to set up the duplicate condition.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create an administrator account referencing a non-existent or invalid permission_id. Should fail and return a validation or integrity error. Validates referential integrity for permission assignments.

Test updating an administrator's permission_id and name fields. Scenario covers the ability of an authorized administrator to assign new permission roles or update display name, and checks that the returned record reflects the changes and audit log updates are created.

dependencies.purpose: Creates the administrator to be updated and provides target UUID.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update an administrator using a non-existent administratorId. Should result in a 404 not found or validation error, verifying robust error management for bad UUIDs.
Attempt to update an administrator profile using insufficient permissions (non-admin or general user role). Expects access denied error and no update to occur in database or audit logs.

dependencies.purpose: Creates the administrator as update target.

scenario.draft: Test successful hard deletion of an administrator account by its UUID as a super-admin or permission manager. Covers pre-test creation of a target admin and verifies actual row removal and audit log recording. Also ensures no roles or permissions are left orphaned.

dependencies.purpose: Creates the target administrator to ensure known UUID for deletion.

scenario.draft: Test proper error handling when attempting to delete a non-existent administrator UUID. Should result in a 404 not found. Validates that system prevents phantom deletes and integrity is preserved.

Try to delete an administrator while logged in as a user lacking super-admin or admin-management privileges. System must deny the operation and return a clear error, with no backend mutation or deletion occurring.

dependencies.purpose: Provides the UUID of an existing administrator to attempt deletion on.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of all available RBAC permission/role definitions by an administrator. Validates that the correct role structures (code, display name, description) are returned and no sensitive data beyond what is allowed in the permission schema is exposed.
Attempt to fetch the list of permissions without administrator role (e.g., as a customer or seller). Expects access denial or permission error, validating role-based access control is enforced.

Test the ability to search product categories with a keyword filter and pagination. First, ensure there are categories with different names and hierarchical depths in the system by creating categories as a seller (dependency). As an administrator, perform a PATCH search requesting a page with a specific name keyword and check that only matching categories are returned and pagination metadata is correct. Verify that categories not matching the keyword are excluded. Also test searches by parent_id and depth to confirm that hierarchy filtering works. Validation: confirms only allowed roles can perform this search and filters/sorting adhere strictly to business/configuration rules. Edge cases: search with no matches, search with invalid parameters, and role-based access violation.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple categories with diverse names, parents, and depths to setup data for keyword, parent, and depth based search testing.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving the detail of a product category as a customer by supplying a valid categoryId. First, create a category as a seller to obtain a valid UUID (dependency). Then, perform a GET as a customer with this UUID and verify all expected atomic fields are present and correct. Also, attempt to fetch a category with a malformed or non-existent identifier to confirm the API returns error responses (404 or validation error). Checks that category visibility rules and permissions work: customer roles should only be able to view allowed categories and get proper error feedback for restricted or non-existent records.

dependencies.purpose: Create a category to ensure there is a valid categoryId to test detail retrieval as a customer.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a category's detail as a seller using a valid categoryId, and validate access rights. First, create a category as the seller (dependency) and attempt to fetch its details; check that all fields returned match what was created. Then attempt to fetch a category created by another seller or a non-existent categoryId, verifying that error responses are received (404 or 403 as applicable) and that the access and visibility rules are correctly enforced for the seller role.

dependencies.purpose: Create a category as the seller to ensure there is an owned categoryId for valid access tests and to simulate unowned category scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test administrator retrieval of any product category by categoryId, regardless of visibility. First, create categories with various visibility and parent/child relationships as a seller (dependency). As an admin, GET detail for several valid UUIDs and check that all data is returned, including categories that are not visible to customers. Also, try with non-existent and invalid UUIDs to assure 404 or validation errors are returned. Verify that only administrators/privileged roles can access this detail and error if insufficient permissions. This ensures RBAC enforcement and correct error scenarios are handled.

dependencies.purpose: Create categories (including hidden or special admin-only categories) as test data for admin retrieval scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test seller ability to create a new product category via POST. Provide required atomic fields (unique name, optional parent_id, depth). First, successfully create a new category and verify all returned fields (id, depth, parent_id, etc.) match input and system rules. Next, attempt to create another category with the same name under the same parent to provoke a uniqueness constraint violation—expect a conflict or descriptive error. Also, test creating with a parent_id that does not exist (should return an error). Business logic: Only sellers/administrators can create; category names must be unique within a parent. Check for correct enforcement and error feedback in all cases.

Test failure cases when creating a category as a seller: omit required fields, supply invalid data (such as a name that's too long or contains invalid characters), or use unauthorized roles. Confirm that proper validation errors are returned, and permissions are enforced. This validates schema conformance and business rules for input sanitation and RBAC.

Test creating a subcategory by referencing an existing parent category. First, create a root category as the seller (dependency). Use its ID as the parent_id when creating a new category and ensure the response reflects correct parent/child linkage and increased depth. Edge cases: attempt to create a subcategory with a parent at max allowed depth or with an invalid parent reference, confirming correct errors are returned and system hierarchy rules are preserved.

dependencies.purpose: Create a root category first to serve as the parent for the subcategory creation test.

scenario.draft: Verify that an administrator can successfully update an existing behavioral tracking event for a customer. Begin by creating a customer account, then create a valid behavioral tracking record for that customer. Attempt to update the event's classification and payload via PUT, providing new event data. Confirm that the API returns the updated record reflecting provided changes, and that all audit and permission requirements are followed.

dependencies.purpose: Create the target customer account for which behavioral tracking will be managed.
Create a sample behavioral tracking record to set up for update.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a behavioral tracking entry for a customer as a non-administrator (e.g., as a regular customer or with insufficient privileges). Expect the API to deny the request with an unauthorized or forbidden error. Confirm that unauthorized users cannot update another user's tracking events, enforcing privacy and compliance policies.

dependencies.purpose: Register the target customer account to use for attempted activity.
Ensure the behavioral tracking event exists for the customer.

scenario.draft: Test the scenario where an administrator attempts to update a behavioral tracking event for a customer, but the specified behaviorTrackingId does not exist. The API should return a not found (404) error. Confirm proper error message and that no unrelated data is modified.

Confirm that the created post appears in global post listings and that audit/tracking fields (timestamps, author) are auto-populated accordingly.

Test an administrator creating a post and verify that all admin-required fields are accepted. After creation, retrieve the post using the get detail endpoint to ensure administrative posts are created and retrievable through normal flows, and are attributed correctly to the admin role.

scenario.draft: Test updating a post as an administrator using a non-existent postId. Confirm the response is a not found error and no new content is created or altered.

scenario.draft: Try deleting a non-existent post (invalid postId) as a seller. Expect a not found error, and verify the system does not alter any other post records.
