scenario.draft: Verify a seller can create a new SKU for a product they own. Seller logs in, provides unique sku_code and valid data, and submits to endpoint. SKU is added and can be retrieved. Dependencies: Seller and a product under that seller must already exist.

dependencies.purpose: Create seller account (for authentication/authorization).
Create product owned by seller (to get productId).

scenario.draft: Seller attempts to create a SKU with an already existing sku_code for the same product. This should trigger a validation constraint error, preventing duplicate SKUs. Dependencies: Seller, product, and one initial SKU must exist. Attempt creation of a second SKU with duplicate code.

dependencies.purpose: Create seller.
Create product under seller.
Create first SKU for the product.

scenario.draft: Verify that a customer (logged-in or guest) can retrieve a full, normalized list of all product taxonomy categories. The expected result is a list containing all categories, including their hierarchical structure (parent_id, depth, name). Confirm there are no extraneous or denormalized fields, and only active (non-deleted) categories are included. Test typical user flows such as displaying the category selector for browsing or filtering products.

Attempt to access the category list as a role that lacks proper authorization (e.g., send an invalid or expired token, or use an unexpected role). Verify that the system denies access (if configured as such), or restricts the returned data to public/allowed categories. Check that proper error responses or scoping rules are enforced in accordance with business requirements.

Verify that a seller (authenticated) can retrieve the complete list of product taxonomy categories, with parent/child hierarchy as per the schema. Ensure that the seller receives results similar to customers but may also include hidden/system categories if their role allows it. This scenario supports seller catalog management, including category selection during product creation.

Attempt to access category listing as a seller whose account is suspended or whose permissions are limited. Confirm that the API restricts visibility according to the seller's role/permission configuration, either via error response or by scoping out restricted categories.

Verify that an administrator can fetch the complete list of all categories including those that might be hidden from customer/seller views (e.g., system categories, inactive categories, or those reserved for special purposes). Confirm all hierarchical relationships are correctly represented, and all atomic fields per schema are present. This scenario enables admin taxonomy management workflows.

Test the response when an unauthorized user (e.g., an expired admin token or insufficient privileges) attempts to access the admin category list. Validate that access is denied and a proper authorization error is returned according to policy.

Test category advanced search as a customer with various filters (e.g., partial name match, depth, parent_id, pagination parameters). Verify that the filtered, paginated result only contains categories matching the search criteria, and that pagination metadata is correctly supplied. Also, ensure users cannot filter for hidden system categories unless authorized. This scenario supports category selector UIs with search-for-category capabilities.

Attempt to search categories with advanced criteria as a customer having invalid credentials or improper permissions (e.g., restricted/blocked customer, expired token). Confirm that the API responds appropriately (error or limited results), enforcing business rules and privacy constraints.

Send an invalid or malformed search/filter payload as a customer (e.g., non-existent depth value, invalid parent_id format, or malformed pagination). Verify that the API returns a validation or format error and does not proceed with the query.

Verify that a seller can use advanced search/filter on product categories, such as searching by partial name, filtering by levels (depth), parent category, or using pagination/sorting options. Confirm that the results match the specified criteria, correct pagination is returned, and hidden/system categories are only visible if permitted by role. This supports seller-side UIs with category search forms.

Attempt to perform advanced search as a seller whose account is suspended, using invalid credentials, or whose permission level does not allow category search. Ensure the API restricts access, returning proper error responses or empty result sets as defined by security policies.

Provide the advanced category search endpoint with invalid input—such as a malformed parent_id, invalid depth, or incorrect pagination structure. Confirm that validation errors are raised, and no data is returned until the input is corrected. This verifies input validation and error handling in advanced search forms.

Verify that a customer can successfully soft-delete their own comment on a post. Register a customer, log in, create a post as the customer, add a comment as the post author or another customer account. Then, perform a DELETE request on the comment as the authoring customer. Validate that the comment's 'deleted_at' field is set, and it no longer appears in normal comment queries for the post.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new test customer to act as the author of the comment.
Create a new community post to which the comment will be added.
Create a new comment under the post to be soft-deleted.

scenario.draft: Verify that a customer cannot soft-delete a comment made by another user. Register two customer accounts. Have Customer A create a post and comment under it. Try to delete this comment using Customer B's credentials. The DELETE should fail with a forbidden (403) error, and the comment remains undeleted.

dependencies.purpose: Register Customer A and Customer B for role separation.
Customer A creates a post to allow downstream actions.
Customer A creates a comment to later be tested for deletion.

scenario.draft: Test the API's response when attempting to soft-delete a comment that has already been deleted. Register a customer, create a post and comment, then delete the comment. Attempt to delete it again, expecting a clean error or idempotent behavior, and ensure no change in the audit trail or state.

dependencies.purpose: Register customer for comment authorship.
Create a post to which a comment will be attached.
Create a comment to then delete and re-delete.
Perform the initial soft-delete on the comment.

scenario.draft: Verify that a seller or administrator can soft-delete any comment under a post for moderation purposes. Register a seller, create a post and two comments (one by the seller, one by a customer), then as the seller perform a DELETE on both comments. Confirm their soft-deletion by checking the deleted_at fields and audit logs.

dependencies.purpose: Prepare or verify seller role for authenticated actions.
Create a post as a seller.
Create comments for the post as both seller and another account for moderation test.

scenario.draft: Verify that an administrator can soft-delete any comment regardless of author for moderation or compliance reasons. Register (or use) an administrator, create a post and comment as a customer, then as the admin, DELETE the comment. Confirm via get (admin endpoint) that deleted_at is populated and the comment no longer lists in normal post comment queries.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure administrative account is authenticated for privileged actions.
Create a customer-authored post to which a comment is attached.
Create a comment as a customer to be deleted by admin.

scenario.draft: Verify that a customer can successfully retrieve a list of all attachments associated with a post they own or have access to. Register a customer, create a post, add multiple attachments, and perform a GET on the attachments endpoint. Check that all added attachments are returned with correct metadata and file URIs.

dependencies.purpose: Register the test customer who will create the post and attachments.
Create a post as the customer.
Upload several attachments (files/media) to the post to provide retrieval content.

scenario.draft: Attempt to retrieve attachments for a postId that does not exist or that the customer does not have access to. Confirm API returns 404 (not found) or a suitable access error, and no attachment data is returned.

Ensure that a seller can retrieve all attachments for a post they own or moderate. Register as a seller, create a post, upload attachments, then GET the list of attachments. The response should include all proper metadata for uploaded files, and must not expose unauthorized attachments.

dependencies.purpose: Prepare or verify seller account for authentication.
Seller creates a post.
Upload one or more attachments as the seller.

scenario.draft: Test the successful creation of a new product bundle by an administrator. First, create two valid product records using the administrator endpoint (one as the bundle master, one as a component). Then call the bundle creation endpoint, associating the master product with the component product, specifying required-ness and a minimum quantity. Verify that the response includes all persisted bundle fields and references the correct master/component products. Ensure the bundle respects business constraints (products must exist; duplicate bundle composition is not permitted).

dependencies.purpose: Create the product that will serve as the bundle master.
Create the product that will be included as a bundled component.

scenario.draft: Test the failure case of attempting to create a product bundle where the specified component product does not exist. Create a valid bundle master product first. Attempt to create a bundle referencing a random UUID as the component product. The system should respond with a validation error indicating the component product does not exist, preventing bundle creation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid bundle master product record for assignment as the bundle group.

scenario.draft: Demonstrate successful update of a product bundle by the owning seller. First, create a seller, authenticate, and create two products under the seller, then bundle them together. Update the bundle's quantity and required-ness fields. Confirm that the update is reflected in the persisted bundle entity and audit logs, and ensure business rules are enforced (e.g., a bundle cannot be updated to reference an unrelated component, etc).

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller account for owning products and bundles.
Create and assign the bundle master product to the seller.
Create and assign the bundle component product to the seller.
Establish the initial product bundle relation as a prerequisite for updating.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a product bundle, changing the component to a product not owned by the seller. Ensure the API rejects this change with a permission or business rule violation error, confirming that sellers can only bundle their own products.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller for bundle ownership.
Create seller-owned products.
Create a product outside the seller's ownership (via admin) to use as an invalid component.
Create an initial valid bundle to be updated.

scenario.draft: Test update of a product bundle by an administrator, modifying fields such as required-ness and component quantity. Ensure the administrator is able to perform updates regardless of seller ownership. Confirm system enforces business rules, such as quantity must be positive, component products must exist, and relationships are still valid after the update.

dependencies.purpose: Create the master product for the bundle by admin.
Create the component product for the bundle by admin.
Create the initial bundle between master and component.

scenario.draft: Test successful hard deletion of a product bundle by the owning seller. Begin by creating a seller, their two products, and a product bundle between them. Then delete the product bundle and ensure it is no longer returned in queries from the product bundles endpoint. Ensure linked products remain unaffected and only the bundle relationship is removed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller for ownership context.
Create both master and component products for the seller.
Create the product bundle to later delete.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a product bundle that does not exist, using a random UUID for productBundleId. Expect a 404 not found error, with a clear error message and no side effects on other bundles or products.

dependencies.purpose: Create seller for associating product context.
Create at least one product for context to use as the master.

scenario.draft: Demonstrate administrator's ability to delete any product bundle regardless of product ownership. Create two products and a bundle as prerequisites, then execute a hard delete for the bundle using the admin endpoint. Verify deletion and that the product and any unrelated bundles remain untouched.

dependencies.purpose: Create admin-owned product for master.
Create component product under admin.
Create the specified product bundle for deletion.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a non-existent product bundle as an administrator using an invalid (random) productBundleId. Confirm that the system returns an appropriate error (404 not found), and no unintended deletions or system changes occur.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure admin has at least one product to use as a valid master product context.

scenario.draft: Verify that an administrator can successfully filter and paginate comments for a specific post using a range of search criteria (such as keyword in body, author, visibility, and date ranges). Set up a post with several comments from multiple users, including some private comments and different creation timestamps. Then, as admin, use the PATCH endpoint with different combinations of search parameters and verify that the returned comments match the criteria, correct comments are included/excluded according to privacy and status, and pagination metadata is accurate.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new community post to serve as the target for adding multiple comments.
Add various comments to the created post, authored by different users, with a mix of public/private flags and spread out timestamps to ensure effective filtering.

scenario.draft: Validate that a customer can retrieve the detail for a public comment on a post, and that access is denied for private comments not owned by the customer. Create a post and at least two comments, one public and one private (owned by different users). Try retrieving both comments as another user. Expect a 200 status and correct data for public; 404 or access error for private (if not owned).

dependencies.purpose: Create a new community post to use as a container for comments.
Add two comments (public and private) to the post under different user contexts for realistic access control testing.

scenario.draft: Check that querying a commentId that does not exist under a valid postId returns a not found (404) error. Create a post and attempt to GET a comment with a random UUID not present for that post. Confirm proper error handling and messaging.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a known, valid postId to use in the non-existent commentId lookup.

scenario.draft: Ensure that a seller can retrieve the detail of a comment on a post they do not own only when access rules permit (e.g., if the comment is public). Confirm correct error for access-denied on private or restricted comments not authored by them. Create a post (by another user) and comments (public/private) to verify role-based data access, using a seller session for GET attempts.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as a customer user, not as the seller, to test access boundaries.
Add comments to the post with various privacy settings for testing seller-side comment access.

scenario.draft: Administrators must be able to retrieve the details for any comment on a post, regardless of privacy flag or deletion status, for auditing and moderation. Create a post, add several comments (some marked private, some soft-deleted) and verify the admin can access them all. Confirm correct fields for deleted or private comments.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to host comments covering all visibility cases.
Add several comments under different privacy settings and then soft delete at least one to check admin reach.
Soft-delete a comment to verify admin visibility for delete case.

scenario.draft: Test that a customer can successfully create a new comment under a post with valid body, privacy flag, and that the comment is returned with correct metadata. Confirm that comment is marked as pending moderation if business rules apply. Attempt comment creation as both post author and a non-author. Validate anti-abuse rules if present.

dependencies.purpose: Generate a post to serve as the comment target. Owner and non-owner will both try commenting.

scenario.draft: Verify that comment creation fails with appropriate error messages when required body fields are missing, body is too short, or if invalid privacy flags are set. Attempt to submit incomplete or invalid data for a comment and check that the API enforces schema and business rules strictly.

dependencies.purpose: Prepare a post to target for invalid comment creation attempts.

scenario.draft: Test successful deletion of an external account by an administrator. Precondition: A customer account exists with at least one external account linked (e.g., Google). The administrator performs the delete operation for a specific external accountId and customerId. Verify that the external account is removed, proper audit logs are recorded, and the account no longer appears in queries. This is irreversible and should confirm permissions and referential cleanup.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test customer account for setup.
Link a new external account to the test customer to ensure there is an externalAccountId to delete.

scenario.draft: Test failure when attempting to delete a non-existent external account. Precondition: Administrator tries to delete an externalAccountId that does not exist for a valid customerId. Expect a 404 Not Found error and verify appropriate error structure in response and no side-effects.

dependencies.purpose: Create customer as context to test non-existent externalAccountId scenario.

scenario.draft: Test that users who are not administrators (e.g., regular customers) cannot delete external accounts via the administrator endpoint. Attempt the DELETE operation as a non-admin and expect a permission (403) denial response.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer who will attempt the forbidden operation.
Link an external account for testing restricted access.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of all behavioral tracking records for a customer. Precondition: Customer exists with at least two logged behavior tracking events (such as login and product view). The customer authenticates and performs the GET request. Expect all records to be retrieved, matching the created events, and only the authenticated owner can access this list.

dependencies.purpose: Register a test customer.
Log multiple behavioral events for the customer before retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test failure scenario when attempting to retrieve another customer's behavioral tracking events. Precondition: Two customers exist. Customer A attempts to fetch Customer B's behaviorTrackings via GET. Expect a 403 Forbidden error to ensure privacy and data isolation.

dependencies.purpose: Register Customer A.
Register Customer B.
Log at least one behavioral event for Customer B for retrieval attempt by Customer A.

scenario.draft: Test successful administrative retrieval of all behavior trackings for a specific customer. Precondition: At least one customer exists with multiple behavioral events logged. Administrator logs in and performs the GET operation. Verify all customer events are returned and audit logs reflect the access.

dependencies.purpose: Register a test customer.
Log behavioral events for the customer before admin access.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when administrator tries to retrieve behavior trackings for a non-existent customerId. Expect an appropriate error (404 Not Found) and confirm there is no data leakage or unexpected side-effect.

Test filtered, paginated search for a customer's behavioral tracking records as the owner. Precondition: Several behavior tracking events exist with varying event_type and timestamps. The customer performs a PATCH with criteria filtering on event_type and date range. Expect only matching events and correct pagination metadata in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create the test customer.
Generate a variety of tracking events for filter/pagination testing.

scenario.draft: Test paginated search for behavioral events at a pagination boundary (e.g., requesting a page past the available data). Precondition: A known number of events are present (e.g., 7), the user requests a page with a high offset/limit that results in an empty data array and correct pagination info. No errors or data leakage should occur.

dependencies.purpose: Setup a customer.
Log a specific number of tracking events for pagination test.

scenario.draft: Test administrator-initiated search with advanced filter criteria for a customer's behavioral tracking events. Precondition: Several events of different types exist for the customer. Admin performs PATCH with filter criteria for event_type and a custom time window. Expect only filtered results and full pagination in response.

dependencies.purpose: Create customer record for advanced search.
Log various tracking events for the customer.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when performing PATCH search on a non-existent customerId as admin. Expect a 404 or similar error response, confirm error details, and ensure the operation does not return data for invalid ids.

Verify that an administrator can successfully fetch the full details of a coupon redemption record using a valid couponRedemptionId. Start by ensuring there is an existing coupon redemption record in the database, which is typically created through a normal customer redemption process or via the coupon and campaign issuance workflow. The test should confirm that all detail fields are returned, including coupon/campaign association, redemption status, associated customer, order/product target, timestamp, and result outcome. Critical business rules such as matching the provided couponRedemptionId with an existing log must be validated. This test verifies the operation's necessity for backoffice support, fraud investigation, and compliance workflows.

dependencies.purpose: Create or ensure existence of a coupon redemption record with a valid couponRedemptionId for lookup.

scenario.draft: Attempt to retrieve a coupon redemption detail using a couponRedemptionId that does not exist in the database. The expected behavior is that the endpoint returns a not-found error, confirming that the system does not leak information about non-existent or invalid redemption logs. This is crucial for security and compliance. This test validates the not-found case and appropriate error messaging to the administrator.

Verify access control by attempting to fetch a coupon redemption record detail with a user role that is not an administrator. The endpoint should deny access, returning an authorization error and preventing data leakage. This test ensures only privileged admin/support personnel can inspect sensitive redemption analytics and logs.

Verify that a customer can retrieve all comments for a given active product review. First, authenticate as a customer and create a new review for a product to obtain its reviewId, then post several comments (including public and private) to that review (using the comments create endpoint). Retrieve the comments using this GET endpoint and assert all non-deleted, visible comments are included. Confirm proper fields are returned and privacy rules are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create a customer-owned product review to obtain a valid reviewId for testing.
Post at least one public and one private comment to the review for listing test.

scenario.draft: Attempt to list comments for a review that has been soft-deleted (deleted_at set). Authenticate as a customer, create a review, post at least one comment, then soft-delete the review using the erase endpoint. Call the GET endpoint for comments and verify that the API returns the proper error or empty set, in accordance with business rules for deleted resources.

dependencies.purpose: Create the review for test setup.
Post comments to the review.
Soft delete the review to simulate deleted resource scenario.

scenario.draft: Test that customers cannot access comments for reviews they do not own, or for private comments belonging to others. As customer A, create a review and post a private comment. As customer B, attempt to retrieve comments for customer A's review, and assert that private comments are not visible, and other restrictions apply. API should not leak private or unauthorized comment data.

dependencies.purpose: Customer A creates a review.
Customer A creates private comment to review.

scenario.draft: As an authenticated seller, retrieve the comments for a review left on one of their products. Seller creates a product, a customer submits a review, then posts several comments (public and private). The seller queries the comments. Confirm that the seller can see all comments per their permissions, including private comments where allowed (for their product only), and that correct details are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product as a seller to receive reviews.
Customer submits a review of the seller's product.
Post public and private comments for the review.

scenario.draft: Verify that a seller cannot retrieve comments for a review on a product not owned by them. Seller A creates a product, Customer reviews and comments, but Seller B tries to retrieve comments via this endpoint. The API must deny or mask access to unauthorized data, returning an error or empty result per business policy.

dependencies.purpose: Seller A creates a product.
Customer reviews Seller A's product.
Customer posts comments.

scenario.draft: Confirm that an administrator can list all comments for any review, regardless of review owner or comment privacy. As admin, query comments for a customer-owned review to check that all comments (public, private, and soft-deleted if business policy allows) are returned. Verify compliance with audit and privacy requirements, and assert full data returned for moderation or investigation use cases.

dependencies.purpose: Create customer review for test target.
Post multiple comments with varying privacy and deletion status.

scenario.draft: Test successful soft deletion of a product review by its author. Customer creates a new review, verifies its existence, then invokes the erase endpoint. Check that deleted_at is set, the review is hidden in normal queries, and subsequent attempts to update or delete again are handled correctly (error or no-op as per business rule).

dependencies.purpose: Create a review as the test subject to obtain reviewId.

scenario.draft: Attempt to soft-delete a review as a customer who is not the owner. Customer A creates a review, Customer B attempts to delete it using this endpoint. Verify that access is denied and the review is not deleted, ensuring that ownership checks are strictly enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Customer A creates a review for negative permission testing.

scenario.draft: As an administrator, soft-delete any product review in the system (regardless of owner). First create a review as a customer, then as admin call the erase endpoint on that reviewId. Assert deleted_at is set and review is hidden in normal queries, but available in admin queries as required. This tests administrative compliance flows and privilege enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create review to be deleted by admin as test target.

scenario.draft: As an administrator, attempt to delete a reviewId that does not exist in the system. Verify that the endpoint responds with a proper not found error, and no other resources are affected. This checks error handling and system integrity for destructive admin operations.

Test retrieval of immediate child categories under a specified parent category by UUID. Create a root category first, then create several child categories beneath it using the category creation endpoint to ensure a populated hierarchy. Invoke this endpoint to list immediate children and validate that only the direct child categories are returned, with correct parent_id reference, depth value, and all relevant fields as per schema. This scenario checks the correct hierarchical result, and handles cases where the parent has children and when the parent has no children (should return an empty array).

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent category to act as the root for this test.
Create one or more child categories nested under the parent for retrievability validation.

scenario.draft: Test error scenario when attempting to list immediate child categories under a non-existent parent category UUID. Use a random UUID not present in the database. The system should return a not found error response indicating the parent category does not exist. This tests API validation for invalid path parameters and absence handling.

Test that only users with administrator or seller role are allowed to use this operation. Attempt to access the endpoint as an unauthorized user (e.g., customer role or unauthenticated). The API must enforce access control and return a forbidden error. Then, re-run as an authorized admin/seller and validate successful listing.

Test that a seller can successfully list immediate child categories for a given parent category they are authorized to access. Create the parent and at least two child categories under this parent. Validate that only direct children are shown in the response and that their parent_id fields match the parent. This confirms proper hierarchical assignments for the seller context.

dependencies.purpose: Create a root category as a seller.
Create multiple child categories under the parent for the hierarchy.

scenario.draft: Test scenario where the requested parent category exists but has no child categories. After creating a parent category with no children, make the call and confirm the API returns an empty array while returning correct parent metadata. This ensures graceful handling of empty child situations.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent category as seller for which no children will be created.

scenario.draft: Test permission enforcement by attempting to access this endpoint as a customer role or unauthorized user. The request should fail with a forbidden error. This validates proper RBAC protection is in place for seller category listing.

Test successful paginated and filtered retrieval of child categories as an administrator. First, create a parent category and several child categories with varying names and depths. Use filtered search criteria in the request body (such as partial name matching, depth, or custom sort fields) and pagination controls (limit/offset). Validate that the API returns only the matching child categories, paginated accordingly, and with accurate page counts and sorting.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a parent category for child creation.
Add a number of child categories with different names or properties.

scenario.draft: Test searching for child categories with a filter that does not match any records under the given parent category. The API should return an empty data array with correct pagination metadata. This tests both the filtering logic and graceful handling of empty result sets.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a parent category for a clean test context.

scenario.draft: Test that only administrator and seller roles can use the PATCH child categories endpoint. Attempt a request as an unauthorized user (e.g., customer or unauthenticated session), and validate that the API responds with forbidden or unauthorized error. This tests RBAC enforcement.

Test advanced filtering and pagination of child categories as a seller. Prepare a parent category, then create several children with different names and other filterable fields. Use filters (partial name, depth, etc) and pagination parameters in the request body, and verify only appropriate records are returned, along with expected page metadata. Validate that the results are limited to children of the correct parent and match the filtering parameters.

dependencies.purpose: Create the relevant parent category as a seller.
Insert multiple child categories with varied properties.

scenario.draft: Test searching for child categories under a non-existent or unauthorized parent_category_id as a seller. The API should return a not found or forbidden error as appropriate. This scenario checks for error handling for invalid resource references and access rights.

Test that only sellers and administrators can use this endpoint. Attempt the request as a non-seller (e.g., customer), expecting a forbidden or unauthorized error. This validates that proper access controls are applied for PATCH on seller category children.

Test retrieving full detail for a specific child category under a known parent category using both UUIDs. Set up the hierarchy by creating a parent category, then a child category under it. Use this endpoint to fetch the child's details, and verify all fields, including id, parent_id, name, depth, and schema attributes, are correctly returned and that the parent_id matches the parent. The test validates parent-child linkage and record completeness.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent category for the hierarchy.
Create the child category to retrieve in the scenario.

scenario.draft: Test error handling for detail retrieval with invalid or mismatched parent and/or child category UUIDs. Try non-existent parent/child UUIDs and correct parent with wrong child, or vice versa. Validate that the response returns a not found error ensuring the linkage is required and cannot be bypassed. This protects tree integrity.

Ensure that only administrators and sellers can retrieve child category details via this endpoint. Attempt access as a customer or unauthorized user, and verify the API properly restricts access, responding with a forbidden or unauthorized error. This tests RBAC enforcement for child category detail retrieval.

Test the creation of a new media snapshot (photo/media) attached to a seller's community post. Set up: Register/login a seller, create a post as the seller to obtain postId. Attempt to create a snapshot with a valid media URI, optional caption, and post linkage. Validate that the returned entity is stored, fields are correct, and that permissions are enforced such that only authenticated users can create snapshots. Expected outcome: snapshot is created, attached to the post, and all data matches input. Error scenario: attempt with missing/invalid postId or media_uri should fail with appropriate error.

dependencies.purpose: To create a new post as a seller and obtain a valid postId for snapshot attachment.

scenario.draft: Test the creation of a snapshot (photo/media) by an administrator on an existing post. Prepare by registering as an administrator and creating a post to get a postId. First, attempt creation using valid media_uri and confirm that all normalized fields are correctly set. Second, attempt to create a snapshot with missing/invalid media_uri or linking to a non-existent postId and verify that the operation fails with clear validation or foreign key errors. Document permission boundary so that only administrators (or permitted users) can create snapshots via this route.

dependencies.purpose: Create a community post as an administrator before attaching a snapshot.

scenario.draft: Test updating details (e.g., caption or media_uri) of an existing snapshot for a post as the owning customer. Set up: Register/login as a customer, create a post, add a snapshot, then update that snapshot. Expected: The update call should succeed and fields should be changed. Negative: attempt to update a snapshot not owned by the customer, or supply an invalid postId/snapshotId, should result in error or permission denial.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as a customer to obtain postId.
Attach a snapshot to the post as the customer and obtain snapshotId before updating.

scenario.draft: Test updating an existing snapshot’s fields (caption or media_uri) on a post as the owning seller. Scenario: Seller creates a post, attaches a snapshot, and performs an update on the snapshot. Confirm successful updates and field changes. Also validate: attempt to update with an invalid snapshotId/postId or as a different user fails as expected with an error. Edge case: try to supply an update for non-editable fields and confirm these are ignored or cause errors as defined by business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new post as seller to obtain postId.
Attach a snapshot as the seller to obtain snapshotId for update.

scenario.draft: Test updating a snapshot attached to a post as the administrator. Admin creates a post and attaches a snapshot, then updates its fields (e.g., caption/media_uri). Confirm that updates are reflected and returns the modified entity. Attempt an update with an invalid postId/snapshotId and verify correct error response. Additional test: try to update the snapshot with missing required fields or invalid input and confirm that validation errors are triggered as expected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as admin and obtain the postId.
Attach a snapshot as admin to obtain snapshotId before update.

scenario.draft: Test that all inventory snapshot records can be successfully retrieved for a valid SKU. First, create a product as an administrator, then add at least one SKU under that product. Insert inventory snapshots for the SKU. Finally, call the GET endpoint with the correct skuId to verify all inventory change snapshots are returned as expected, including edge cases where multiple snapshots exist or none are present.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new product to associate with the SKU.
Create a SKU associated with the newly created product.
Log one or more inventory change snapshots for the SKU to ensure there is data to retrieve.
