Test creating a new community snapshot as an administrator with all required fields (media_uri, optional caption, linked post_id/product_id/customer_id). Confirm response returns the created snapshot entity with all atomic fields correctly persisted. Also validate that unique constraints and required fields are enforced, appropriate audit logs are triggered, and the created snapshot can be immediately retrieved with GET by id for round-trip validation.

Test creating a new community snapshot with a missing required field (such as omitting media_uri). Expect the API to reject the request with a clear validation error specifying the missing field(s) and to not create a record. No partial records should be persisted.

Test updating mutable metadata of a community snapshot (such as updating the caption or correcting the media_uri) as an administrator. Steps: create a snapshot, then send a PUT request to update allowed fields. Confirm that only allowed fields are changed, all others are left unchanged, and the updated timestamp is correctly set. Verify changes are reflected in subsequent GET queries.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new snapshot for update scenario and to provide a valid snapshotId.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a snapshot using an invalid or non-existent snapshotId. Expect a not found error with no update action performed. Database state must be unchanged, and error logs/audit events are generated as required.

Attempt to update immutable or protected fields (if any) of a community snapshot (such as trying to change system-generated IDs) as administrator. The API should reject these with proper validation errors and not alter persistent data.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a new snapshot as update target to validate rejection of immutable-field updates.

scenario.draft: Test deleting a snapshot as an administrator by providing a valid snapshotId. Steps: create a snapshot, then delete it. On successful deletion, the record must be permanently removed; subsequent GET requests to the same id should result in not found. The operation should be logged for audit purposes.

dependencies.purpose: Create a snapshot record for deletion. This will provide a valid snapshotId for the erase scenario.

scenario.draft: Test attempting to delete a snapshot using a nonexistent or previously deleted snapshotId. The API should return a not found error and perform no operation. The error response must not leak internal details to the client.

Simulate an administrator creating a new audit snapshot for an existing order. The test should: (1) create an order as a setup step; (2) make a snapshot creation request with valid required fields according to the IAimallBackendOrderSnapshot.ICreate schema; (3) verify the snapshot is persisted and contents reflect the current state of the order. This supports compliance and audit requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order so that a valid orderId exists to create a snapshot for. This is required for snapshot creation and linking.

scenario.draft: Test creating two audit snapshots for the same order in sequence, verifying that each snapshot correctly reflects the order's state at the respective creation time and that an audit trail is visible. Ensure the second snapshot does not overwrite the first and both can be retrieved.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order for use in sequential snapshot creation.
Create and persist the initial snapshot for the target order before creating a second one.

scenario.draft: Simulate an administrator updating an existing audit snapshot for an order. Steps: (1) create an order; (2) create a snapshot; (3) perform a PUT to update modifiable fields (such as details or note fields) per schema; (4) assert that updated fields reflect the changes and that immutable audit fields remain unchanged. Invalid field attempts or updates on finalized snapshots should yield validation errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order for the test.
Create an initial audit snapshot for the order to obtain orderSnapshotId for update.

scenario.draft: Test successful hard deletion of an audit snapshot by an administrator. Steps: (1) create an order; (2) create a snapshot for that order; (3) perform a DELETE on the snapshot and confirm it is removed from listing endpoints. Attempting to get the deleted snapshot should return a not found error.

dependencies.purpose: Create the order for which we will manage snapshots.
Create the audit snapshot to be deleted.

scenario.draft: Simulate a logged-in customer retrieving the list of their own coupons. Steps include: (1) ensure a customer account exists; (2) ensure at least one coupon is associated with the customer; (3) perform GET to retrieve the coupon list, verifying only the user's coupons are present, and fields match the schema; (4) assert that sensitive fields from other users are never visible.

dependencies.purpose: Create a customer for the test context.
Issue a coupon and associate it with the test customer to verify it appears in the retrieved list.

scenario.draft: Ensure that when a customer with no coupons queries the list endpoint, the returned data is an empty array or page with no coupon entries. This verifies proper permissions and empty state handling for new users or after coupon expiration/deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer to verify the empty case with no associated coupons.

scenario.draft: Simulate an administrator retrieving the complete list of all coupon records in the system. Steps: (1) ensure at least two coupons exist, potentially assigned to different customers; (2) perform the GET request as an administrator; (3) confirm that coupons for all users are listed and critical coupon fields (code, campaign, status) are correctly presented.

dependencies.purpose: Create a system coupon for global listing.
Create a second coupon, possibly linked to an individual customer, to verify diversity in results.

scenario.draft: Attempt to perform the GET request as a non-administrator (such as a regular customer), verifying that the operation is rejected due to insufficient permissions. Ensure an appropriate error is returned and no sensitive coupon data is exposed.

dependencies.purpose: Register a regular customer for the role-based permission check.

scenario.draft: Validate that a seller with valid credentials can successfully update a product they own by providing a valid productId and updated product fields (such as title, description, status, or category). Ensure all changes persist as expected and the response contains the updated product entity. Setup must include a registered seller and an existing product owned by this seller.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller account to own and manage products.
Create a product associated to the seller, so that an update operation can be performed on it.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a product with a non-existent, deleted, or otherwise invalid productId as a seller. Confirm that the API returns an appropriate error (such as 404 not found) and does not alter any data. The seller should otherwise have valid credentials and own other products.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller account to simulate valid seller credentials.

scenario.draft: Simulate a scenario where Seller A attempts to update a product owned by Seller B. Ensure that the API enforces ownership policies and rejects the operation with a permission/authorization error (e.g., 403 forbidden). Both sellers must exist and Seller B must have created the target product.

dependencies.purpose: Create Seller A (attempting unauthorized update).
Create Seller B (the product owner).
Create a product under Seller B ownership.

scenario.draft: Test successful update of any product by an administrator, regardless of seller ownership, by providing valid productId and updated fields. The administrator should be able to update fields such as title, category, or status, and the returned product entity should reflect the changes.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller under whom a product can be registered.
Create a new product to be updated by the administrator.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a product using an invalid or non-existent productId as an administrator. Verify the API responds with an appropriate error code, such as 404 not found, and no product data is changed.

Try to update a product's title as an administrator so that it duplicates an existing product title for the same seller. The API should enforce the uniqueness constraint of seller/title and return a validation error, leaving data unchanged. Setup must ensure two products exist for the same seller with different titles.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller for whom multiple products can be created.
Create Product A for this seller.
Create Product B for this seller with a different title.

scenario.draft: Ensure a seller can permanently delete their own product by providing the correct productId. After the operation, the product should be gone from listings, and any dependent entities should be appropriately handled or removed as per business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create the seller who will own the product.
Create a product, to be later deleted by the owner seller.

scenario.draft: Try to delete a product as Seller A which is owned by Seller B. The API should reject the request with a forbidden error (e.g., 403), ensuring that cross-seller deletion is prevented. Both sellers and the product must be present.

dependencies.purpose: Create Seller A (requestor).
Create Seller B (the product owner).
Create a product under Seller B's ownership.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a product using a non-existent or already deleted productId as a seller. Confirm the system returns an appropriate not found (404) or similar error and does not alter other data.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid seller account to authenticate the request.

scenario.draft: An administrator attempts to delete a valid product. The product should be removed from the catalog, and all related child (dependent) data must be handled according to system cascade or orphan policies. Administrator access is required.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller for product association.
Create a product under the seller; this product will be deleted by the admin.

scenario.draft: Test deleting a product that has assigned options, bundles, or channel assignments as an administrator. System must handle dependent data according to the configured cascade delete or block deletion with an error if constraints are violated. Setup must include at least one dependent child entity.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller for the product.
Create a product to have dependent entities assigned.
Assign at least one product option to the product.

scenario.draft: Given a valid productId, retrieve all product options associated with the product. Confirm that the list matches options added previously, including name and value fields as stored. At least one product option must exist to validate positive retrieval.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller for product and options management.
Create a product to which options will be attached.
Add at least one product option to the created product.

scenario.draft: Attempt to retrieve the option list for a non-existent productId. The API should return a not found error (404), and no data. Setup only needs to ensure the productId used is invalid.
Retrieve options for a product that has no associated product option records. The API should return an empty options list, not an error. Setup must include a valid product with no options created.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller for product management.
Create a product with no attached product options.

scenario.draft: Verify an administrator can successfully delete an attachment from a post. Create a post as a user, attach a file, then as an administrator, call the delete endpoint to remove the attachment. Verify the attachment is no longer listed for the post and cannot be retrieved. Audit logs should reflect the removal.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to which the attachment will be added.
Attach a file to the post so it can later be deleted by the administrator.

scenario.draft: Verify that deleting an attachment with a nonexistent attachmentId returns a clear error. Attempt to delete using a random or already-deleted ID under a valid post, expecting a 404 or similar error response, and audit log entry.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to attempt an invalid attachment deletion against.

scenario.draft: Test that a non-administrator cannot delete an attachment via the admin endpoint. Try as a customer or seller to invoke the DELETE endpoint and verify a permissions or forbidden access error is returned, and the attachment remains present.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post for the permissions test.
Add an attachment to the post to attempt deletion as a non-admin.

scenario.draft: Verify an administrator can retrieve a paginated list of all comments in the system. Create multiple posts and comments, then as administrator, call this GET endpoint and check that response contains all expected comment records with correct pagination and basic fields.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one post that will receive comments.
Add comments to the post for later administrative listing.

scenario.draft: Ensure sensitive or private information is not leaked in the GET response. For private comments or those with privacy flags, verify only permitted fields appear in the admin listing, and check that comments from deleted users do not expose sensitive data.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post.
Add private and public comments for privacy testing.

scenario.draft: Test that an administrator can filter/search comments by author, status (e.g. soft-deleted), and date range. Create multiple comments by different users and at different times, then use PATCH with various filters to ensure only correct comments are returned for each filter type.

dependencies.purpose: Create posts for collecting various comments.
Generate comments by various users and at different times for search testing.

scenario.draft: Check that using a filter known to produce no results (e.g. non-existent author or impossible date range) produces an empty array and correct pagination metadata but no errors.

Verify that an administrator can retrieve all details for a specific comment by its ID, including body, privacy status, and soft-deletion fields. Create a comment first, then call the GET endpoint and assert all schema-defined fields are present.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as a container for the comment.
Create a comment and record its ID for admin detail retrieval.

scenario.draft: Check that an invalid or unauthorized commentId (nonexistent, deleted, or not accessible to the admin) returns the proper error (404/not found or 403/forbidden), and does not leak any comment details.

Validate that a logged-in customer can create a new comment on a post. Ensure all schema-required fields are validated and the returned object matches what was sent, with correct customer and post associations.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post for the comment.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a comment with missing mandatory fields or invalid data (e.g. empty body, illegal privacy flag). Verify the API responds with a clear validation error and no comment is created.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to associate with the comment for validation testing.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a comment using a postId that does not exist, expecting a clear foreign key or not-found error. Confirm the system does not create any comment entry and error message is descriptive.
Ensure a customer cannot create a comment on behalf of another customer by manipulating the author field. Only the authenticated actor should be set as the author, even if spoofed input is provided.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post for the comment.

scenario.draft: Verify that an administrator can permanently delete a file/media attachment from an existing comment. Precondition: Create a customer with a comment and attach a file to it. Action: An administrator performs the delete operation using both commentId and attachmentId. Expected outcome: The attachment is deleted from the comment and database, and further attempts to retrieve it should result in a not-found error. This tests successful authorized deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new comment as a customer to establish the parent comment for the attachment.
Attach a file to the created comment to produce a valid attachmentId for deletion.

scenario.draft: Confirm that a user who is neither the comment's author nor an administrator cannot delete an attachment from a comment. Precondition: A customer creates a comment and attaches a file. Action: A different customer (not the author) attempts to delete the attachment. Expected outcome: The API returns a forbidden error, ensuring only owners or administrators can delete attachments. This validates access control policy.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new comment as the owner customer account.
Attach a file to the created comment.
Attempt deletion as a non-owner (expected to fail due to access control).

scenario.draft: Test that attempting to delete an attachment from a comment, where either the commentId or attachmentId does not exist, results in a not found (404) error. Action: Administrator or comment owner attempts to delete using a random or previously-deleted attachmentId or a commentId that no longer exists. Expected: 404 error indicating the record is not present in the system, ensuring proper error handling for invalid identifiers.

Confirm a customer can retrieve direct replies (child comments) under their parent comment. Precondition: Create a parent comment and post several child comments as replies. Action: Customer retrieves the replies using the GET endpoint. Expected outcome: All active (non-deleted) child comments are returned, sorted as per the implementation, and only visible comments are included. Tests normal listing of threaded discussion.

dependencies.purpose: Create the parent comment as a customer (author or thread starter).
Add multiple child comments as replies under the parent comment.

scenario.draft: Ensure that soft-deleted child comments (where deleted_at is set) are not returned in the result. Precondition: Create a parent comment, add replies, and soft-delete some child comments. Action: List child comments. Expected: Only non-deleted comments appear; soft-deleted comments are excluded from the results, validating compliance and privacy logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create the parent comment as a customer.
Add several child comments (replies).
Soft-delete one or more replies to set deleted_at field.

scenario.draft: Verify that customers can only see child comments for which they have permission, based on privacy settings (is_private). Precondition: Create replies under a parent comment with different privacy flags; some are private, some are public. Action: Another customer attempts to list the child comments. Expected: Only public or permitted comments are visible, private replies from other users are hidden, enforcing privacy.

dependencies.purpose: Create parent comment as customer A.
Create child comments as customer A (private) and as customer B (public/private).

scenario.draft: Ensure an administrator is able to list all child comments (replies) under a parent comment, regardless of privacy flag, including both public and private threads. Precondition: Create parent and child comments with various privacy settings and as different users. Action: Administrator retrieves the child comments. Expected: All replies are returned, reflecting administrator privilege in audit and moderation scenarios.

dependencies.purpose: Create parent comment as a customer for the thread root.
Add replies as various customers with both is_private true and false.

scenario.draft: Ensure that even administrators only receive active, non-soft-deleted comments in list results. Precondition: Create several child comments, then soft-delete some entries. Action: Administrator queries for child comments. Expected: System returns only active (not soft-deleted) comments—demonstrating soft deletion compliance for thread integrity even with admin visibility.

dependencies.purpose: Create parent comment (thread root).
Add multiple child comments (replies).
Soft-delete certain child replies.

scenario.draft: Test searching child comments under a parent thread with filters (e.g., by keyword in body, author ID, privacy, and date). Precondition: Create a parent comment, several replies by different customers, and vary their text and attributes. Action: Customer performs a PATCH search for comments containing a keyword and authored by a specific customer. Expected: Only child comments matching filter criteria are returned, excluding soft-deleted entries.

dependencies.purpose: Create the parent comment as a customer.
Add replies with specific content or author as test data.

scenario.draft: Verify that a customer searching for child comments only receives those they are permitted to view (i.e., public or their own private comments). Precondition: Add replies with a mix of is_private true/false and different authors. Action: Customer B (not owner) uses PATCH to search. Expected: Customer B only receives public comments or their own private comments, not private comments posted by others, ensuring privacy.

dependencies.purpose: Create parent comment.
Create replies with a variety of privacy and author combinations.

scenario.draft: Verify that administrator can perform advanced search and pagination for child comments, filtering by author, privacy status, creation date, and body content. Precondition: Setup parent comment, child comments (including private, public, multiple authors), and query with combined filters. Expected: Administrator has visibility into all child comments, even those private to a specific customer, and can paginate/filter as needed for moderation and audit scenarios.

dependencies.purpose: Create parent comment in the thread to enable replies.
Create replies as various authors with a variety of content and privacy flags.

scenario.draft: Test searching and filtering coupons as a customer using advanced criteria such as coupon code, status (issued, redeemed, expired), campaign association, or issuance/expiry date ranges. Verify that only coupons belonging to the authenticated customer are returned regardless of filter, matching pagination and sorting if specified. Check both cases where results are found and where the filter returns no coupons. Ensure access is denied for any search attempting to access other users' coupons.

dependencies.purpose: Establish a base set of coupons for the authenticated customer prior to applying search and filters.

scenario.draft: Test administrator's ability to search and filter all coupons in the system with combinations of query criteria, such as campaign, status, customer, code, and date ranges. Validate that the result set aligns with the filters and pagination parameters. Confirm that admins see all coupons, including those that are not visible to individual customers. Check that using invalid filters (such as an unsupported status or invalid date range) returns appropriate errors.

dependencies.purpose: Fetch the current global set of coupons to understand the initial state before performing advanced searches.

scenario.draft: Test that an authenticated customer can retrieve complete detail for their own coupon by couponId, receiving all atomic fields: code, campaign, assignment, status, and timestamps. Confirm that the data matches what is stored and is not shared with other customers.

dependencies.purpose: List the customer's coupons to obtain a valid couponId for this detail retrieval scenario.

scenario.draft: Test that an authenticated customer cannot retrieve details for a coupon belonging to a different customer. Attempt to access a couponId not assigned to the user and verify that the system denies access with a suitable error (e.g., 403 forbidden or 404 not found).

dependencies.purpose: Create at least two coupons assigned to different customers, so cross-customer access can be attempted.

scenario.draft: Test that an administrator can retrieve full details for any coupon in the system by couponId, regardless of assignment. Validate that results include all schema fields and cover coupons in various statuses (issued, redeemed, expired).

dependencies.purpose: Get a list of couponIds available in the system for test selection.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a new coupon by an administrator with a unique code and proper campaign association. Ensure required fields are validated and the created coupon appears in the system with correct state and timestamps.

dependencies.purpose: Fetch available discount campaigns to use a valid campaign association in coupon creation.

scenario.draft: Test failure scenario when an administrator attempts to create a coupon with a code that already exists in the system. Verify that uniqueness constraints are enforced and the API returns a conflict error, with no duplicate created.

dependencies.purpose: Create an initial coupon with a known unique code to set up the condition for the duplicate attempt.

scenario.draft: Test the advanced search and paginated retrieval of coupons for a specific discount campaign. Begin by creating a discount campaign and issuing several coupons under this campaign with different statuses (issued, redeemed, expired). Then, use the PATCH endpoint to search for coupons in this campaign filtering by status and expiration date range. Validate that only coupons matching the filter criteria are returned, pagination works, and metadata is accurate. Also ensure that attempting to use filters outside allowed values returns validation errors.

dependencies.purpose: Create a discount campaign to be used for coupon issuance and searching.
Issue several coupons under this campaign with different statuses for search filtering.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving full coupon details by couponId within a discount campaign. First, create a campaign and issue a coupon. Request the coupon's details using the GET endpoint and verify that all expected fields (code, status, assignment, timestamps, campaign linkage, etc.) are returned and correct. Then, attempt to fetch a coupon using a non-existent or invalid couponId to verify that the API returns a proper not-found error and does not expose unrelated data.

dependencies.purpose: Create a campaign to which a coupon can be issued.
Create (issue) a coupon and get its couponId for detail lookup.

scenario.draft: Test the creation of a new coupon under a given discount campaign. First, create a discount campaign. Issue a coupon with valid data (expected fields: code, expiry, status, optional customer assignment). Verify creation returns a correctly structured coupon object. Then, attempt to issue another coupon under the same campaign with a duplicate code and confirm the API enforces uniqueness and returns a duplication error. Additionally, test for invalid payloads (missing required fields or incorrect date formats) and confirm proper validation errors are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a discount campaign to use as parent for coupon creation.

scenario.draft: Test updating a coupon's status and expiry information for a specific coupon within a discount campaign. First, set up a discount campaign and issue a coupon in 'issued' status. Use the PUT endpoint to update the coupon to 'redeemed' or 'expired' status and/or change the expiry date. Validate that state transitions are permitted according to business rules. Also attempt to update a redeemed or invalidated coupon (should be rejected). Finally, test updating with invalid data (e.g., past expiry for issued status) and ensure validation errors are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a discount campaign context.
Issue a coupon to later update its status and expiration.

scenario.draft: Test the deletion (hard delete) of a coupon from a discount campaign. First, create a campaign and issue at least two coupons—one in 'issued' status and one in 'redeemed' or 'expired'. Successfully delete the coupon in 'issued' status and verify it no longer appears in queries or details. Then, attempt to delete a redeemed or expired coupon, confirming the API rejects the request due to business rules. Also, try deleting a non-existent coupon and ensure a not-found error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a discount campaign for coupon issuance.
Issue coupons under the new campaign with appropriate statuses for deletion testing.

scenario.draft: Test the ability of administrators/sellers/customers to search for product review attachments using different filters such as file_type (image/video/doc), file size range, creation date range, or keyword in metadata. Prepare one or more reviews with multiple attachments through the create review and create attachment endpoints. Ensure that the search results honor all specified filter criteria, pagination, and user role restrictions. Validate that only permitted users can see attachment metadata returned by the endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Create a review and obtain its reviewId for conducting attachment operations.
Attach multiple files of varying types and dates to the review to enable effective search/filter scenarios.

scenario.draft: Verify that attempting to search attachments on a non-existent reviewId returns an appropriate error (such as 404 not found). This checks the endpoint's error-handling logic and prevents information leakage for invalid reviews.

Confirm that if search criteria yield no matching attachments (due to overly restrictive filters or empty review), the endpoint returns an empty paginated result set with correct pagination metadata and no errors. This should cover the edge case of searching immediately after review creation but prior to any attachment uploads.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new review with no attachments to test empty search results.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of detailed metadata for a review attachment by its ID, as the uploading customer, a seller, or administrator. Prepare by creating a review, uploading an attachment, and then request its details as the owner and as other permitted roles. Ensure all expected file fields, URIs, types, and metadata are returned and match the original upload. Audit that only permitted roles receive the metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Create a review and obtain its reviewId.
Upload an attachment and obtain its attachmentId for detail testing.

scenario.draft: Verify that a user who is neither the review's owner, the uploading user, nor an authorized administrator/seller cannot access the attachment's metadata. Attempt to request detail from the perspective of a different, unauthorized user—expect an error or forbidden response with no metadata leaked.

dependencies.purpose: Create a review as one user and upload an attachment.

scenario.draft: Test the ability of a seller for the reviewed product to retrieve attachment details for a review, validating role-based access control. The review and attachment should be attributed to a product owned by the seller. Confirm metadata, file URI, and content are visible to the authorized seller, and that restrictions apply for non-related sellers.

dependencies.purpose: Create a review linked to a seller-owned product.
Upload an attachment to the review to obtain attachmentId.

scenario.draft: Test detail retrieval of any product review attachment as an administrator. After any customer has created a review and attached a file, fetch its metadata as admin and assert that all fields are present. Confirm that administrators always have access to attachment details regardless of the uploading customer.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a review and upload at least one attachment.

scenario.draft: Test that a customer can upload a valid attachment to their own product review. This should cover normal (happy path) operation: create a review, upload a file that meets validation (accepted type/size/location), and confirm the created entity matches the input with a valid file URI, type, and metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Create a review and obtain its reviewId for file upload.

scenario.draft: Validate that attempting to upload a file with an unsupported type (e.g., executable) or size exceeding the system threshold is rejected, and an error message identifies the upload policy violation. Review should not have a new attachment as a result of the failed attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Prepare a review for testing by the customer.

scenario.draft: Verify that an administrator can successfully retrieve the metadata for a valid attachment by its unique attachmentId. The workflow is: (1) Create a new post as an administrator or authorized user; (2) Upload a new attachment to the post using the attachments creation endpoint and obtain the attachmentId; (3) Call the GET /administrator/attachments/{attachmentId} endpoint with this ID and confirm all metadata fields are correctly returned; (4) Validate that only metadata and not file content is included, and that all expected fields (file URI, type, size, associated entity references) are present.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post entity to attach the file to; necessary as an attachment must be linked to a post, comment, or review.
Upload the attachment to the created post and receive the attachmentId required for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving attachment metadata using a non-existent or invalid attachmentId. Call the GET /administrator/attachments/{attachmentId} endpoint with a UUID that does not correspond to any attachment and verify that a not-found error or appropriate error message is returned. This checks system error handling for invalid queries.

Test successful creation of an attachment record by submitting valid metadata, including file URI, type, and association with an existing post, comment, or review. The workflow is: (1) Create a post as an administrator to provide a valid parent; (2) Use the POST /administrator/attachments endpoint to register the attachment with correct linkage and file metadata; (3) Validate that the response includes all fields and the persisted metadata matches input. Ensure policy compliance regarding association with an allowed entity type and format of the file URI.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent post to provide a valid entity for attachment association.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create an attachment with a file URI that already exists for the same parent entity, checking for system-enforced uniqueness or expected conflict behavior. Steps: (1) Create and upload an attachment as usual; (2) Attempt a second creation using the same file URI for the same parent entity; (3) Verify that the system returns a conflict or validation error, depending on business rules about file duplication.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post for valid attachment association.
Create the initial attachment for the duplication test.

scenario.draft: Validate system error handling when attempting to create an attachment record linked to a non-existent post, comment, or review. Attempt a POST to /administrator/attachments with either a random UUID as the parent entity or an entity type that doesn't exist. Confirm the system returns a not-found or validation error and does not create a record. This helps prevent orphaned or mislinked attachments.

Test successful update of attachment metadata by an administrator. Process: (1) Create a post and add an attachment to receive a valid attachmentId; (2) Call PUT /administrator/attachments/{attachmentId} to alter metadata (such as file type or description); (3) Confirm system returns updated metadata reflecting the modifications, and that only permitted fields are changed. This verifies both update mechanics and update field restrictions.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post to provide a valid parent for the attachment.
Create an attachment and obtain the attachmentId for update.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update metadata for a non-existent attachmentId. Submit a PUT to /administrator/attachments/{attachmentId} with a random or invalid ID and verify that the system rejects the request with an appropriate not-found or error message. Confirm that no data is changed and error details are returned.

Attempt to update an attachment with a payload that violates business rules or data constraints (e.g., setting an invalid file URI format, file type, or associating to a non-existent entity). Confirm that the API returns a validation error and does not modify the record.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent post for the attachment.
Create a valid attachment as the baseline for submitting invalid update payloads.

scenario.draft: Test hard deletion of an attachment record by its unique attachmentId. Steps: (1) Create a post; (2) Upload a new attachment to obtain attachmentId; (3) Call DELETE /administrator/attachments/{attachmentId} as administrator and confirm that the attachment is removed from the metadata table; (4) Re-attempt fetching the attachment by ID to ensure a not-found error is returned. Confirm that file storage cleanup follows platform policy if applicable, and that deletion event is logged for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as the parent entity.
Upload the attachment and obtain the attachmentId for deletion.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete an attachment with a non-existent attachmentId using the DELETE endpoint. Confirm that the API returns an appropriate error or not-found message and no action is performed on the database. This is critical for auditability and safety of destructive operations.

Verify the ability of an administrator to list all community snapshot records. Steps: (1) Create a post as administrator or authorized user; (2) Upload one or more snapshots linked to the post using the appropriate endpoint; (3) Call GET /administrator/snapshots and confirm the created snapshots appear in the list; (4) Check that metadata fields reflect the correct associations and audit fields (media URI, caption, links).

dependencies.purpose: Create a post entity as the parent for the snapshot.
Upload a snapshot to set up retrievable data.

scenario.draft: Ensure that the GET /administrator/snapshots endpoint returns only metadata fields for each snapshot and does not expose file/media content directly. Steps: (1) Upload a snapshot to a post as an administrator; (2) Fetch the snapshot list; (3) Validate that response entries contain metadata only (media URI, caption, references) and that system security guidelines for content exposure are met.

dependencies.purpose: Create the parent post as context for snapshots.
Upload a snapshot and verify correct listing.

scenario.draft: Attempt to call the GET /administrator/snapshots endpoint as a non-admin user (e.g., customer or seller role) and verify that access is denied with a proper authorization error. This verifies RBAC enforcement on sensitive community media records.
Fetch the list of snapshots when none have been created yet, verifying that the endpoint returns an empty paginated result without errors. This documents initial platform or clean state behavior.

Verify that a platform administrator can permanently delete a channel by its UUID when no dependent records exist. The test first provisions a new channel using the creation API, confirms its existence via detail lookup, and then executes the hard-delete operation. Finally, the scenario queries channel list and channel detail to assert that the channel has been fully removed from the system. Success is defined as the channel no longer being retrievable, with proper audit events logged.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a new unique channel for deletion testing. Returns channelId for use in subsequent steps.
Confirm that the channel exists before deletion. Used both before and after deletion to assert removal.

scenario.draft: Ensure the delete operation fails if the target channel still has section records assigned. Create a channel, add at least one section with the channel as parent, then attempt to hard-delete the channel. Expect the operation to return an error due to foreign key dependency. After the failed deletion, clean up by deleting the section and retry channel delete to verify it now succeeds.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new channel for testing deletion with dependent sections.
Add a section under the created channel to establish a dependency and trigger foreign key constraint.
Clean up the section to allow successful channel deletion, after testing error handling.

scenario.draft: Check that attempting to delete a channel with a non-existent UUID returns a proper 404 error. Use a random UUID not assigned to any channel, attempt the deletion, and verify the correct response is provided without any system disruption.

Test that requesting the list of sections for a channel returns all associated section records. Create a channel and register multiple section entries under it. Call the sections-list API and verify the result contains all created sections with correct attributes and channel linkage.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a new channel to act as parent for the sections.
Add multiple sections to the channel to test multi-record retrieval.

scenario.draft: Verify that searching/filtering for channel sections using pagination and filter criteria returns only the matching sections. Set up a channel with several sections having distinct codes, names, or display order values. Perform search with queries for a specific code, name, or enabled flag, as well as specifying pagination parameters, and assert that returned items match both filter and pagination rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create the channel needed for association with section records.
Create multiple distinct sections under the channel to enable effective filtering and pagination tests.

scenario.draft: Verify that an administrator can successfully retrieve the full details for a section using its channelId and sectionId. Create a channel and a section under it, then request the detail endpoint and ensure all returned fields match the expected values as defined during creation.

dependencies.purpose: Create the parent channel for the section.
Create a new section under the channel to prepare a sectionId to retrieve.

scenario.draft: Test that requesting section details with invalid or mismatched channelId and sectionId returns a 404 not found error. Attempt to fetch a section with a valid channelId but invalid sectionId, and with mismatched parent/child linkage, and validate proper error handling is enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a channel for use in cross-link testing (in case legitimate sectionId is needed).

scenario.draft: Verify that a new section can be successfully created under an existing channel by an administrator. Use unique section code and valid display name attributes, then call the section-creation API and check that the returned entity matches input fields and is correctly assigned to the parent channel.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a new channel to host the test section.

scenario.draft: Validate that creating a section under a channel fails if the section code is not unique within that channel. Add a section to a channel, then attempt to create another section using the same code, and verify the system returns an appropriate error indicating code uniqueness constraint violation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a channel for the section uniqueness test.
Create the initial section using a unique code.

scenario.draft: Verify that a seller (authenticated user) can successfully create a comment on a community post when providing valid required fields. The seller will create or identify a post, then submit a comment with body, is_private flag, and any optional attributes as permitted by the schema. Check that the comment is stored, returned with all fields populated, and associated to the correct postId and author (seller).

dependencies.purpose: A post must exist to comment on. This dependency is fulfilled by the endpoint for creating a post, thereby ensuring the test can target a real postId owned by the seller.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a comment as a seller on a community post but omit required input fields (e.g., missing body). The API should respond with a validation error, rejecting the request and providing appropriate error messages outlining required fields.

dependencies.purpose: A post must exist to comment on, regardless of input error. The seller creates a post to obtain a postId for this scenario.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a comment as a seller on a postId that does not exist (use a non-existent or deleted postId). The API should reject the request with an appropriate error indicating the post was not found or is inaccessible.

Confirm that an administrator can create a comment on any community post by providing all required and optional fields. This includes preparing a post (created by any user type), and then using the admin endpoint to submit a comment (body, is_private, etc.). The response should include the new comment entity, properly linked and all audit fields populated.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure the post exists by having an administrator create a post for reference in this scenario.

scenario.draft: Test the failure scenario where an administrator attempts to create a comment but omits required properties (body, is_private, etc.). The API should return a clear validation error detailing which fields are missing.

dependencies.purpose: Admin creates a post to supply a valid postId for testing comment creation with invalid data.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a comment as admin on a postId that does not exist. The endpoint should respond with a not-found error, as the postId is invalid or deleted.

A customer updates one of their own comments under a specific post, providing valid updates to atomic fields (body, is_private). The update is accepted, reflected in the returned comment entity, and the audit trail is updated. Preconditions: Customer owns the comment, and both post and comment are present and not deleted.

dependencies.purpose: To create a community post for commenting.
Customer creates a new comment on their own post, which is then used for update testing.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a comment for which the customer is not the author (comment created by another user). The API must reject unauthorized edits with a permission error. Preconditions: A comment exists on a post, but a different customer attempts the update operation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as one customer.
Create a comment as a different user to set up a comment not owned by the test customer.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update an existing comment with invalid values (e.g., empty body or illegal data types). The API should return a validation error and reject the update attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Prepare a post for comment creation.
Create a comment as customer so that the update scenario can proceed with invalid data.

scenario.draft: Confirm that a seller can edit their own comment on a given post, updating atomic fields such as body and is_private. The update is reflected in the returned comment entity. Preconditions: Seller creates the post, adds a comment, then updates it.

dependencies.purpose: Seller creates a post for testing comment functionality.
Seller creates a comment on their post, then performs the update operation.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a comment as a seller, but the request body is missing required fields or contains invalid data (e.g., body left blank, non-boolean is_private). The API should respond with a validation error detailing the problem and rejecting the update.

dependencies.purpose: Seller creates a post.
Seller creates a comment to update with erroneous values.

scenario.draft: Verify that a seller cannot update a comment created by another user, customer, or administrator. Attempt to update a comment (not owned by the test seller) and confirm that a permission or access error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Seller creates a post.
Admin creates a comment on the seller's post to ensure ownership mismatch for the test.

scenario.draft: Ensure an administrator can update any comment on a specific post regardless of the original author, provided valid update data (body, is_private) is given. The scenario includes preparing a post and comment (by another user), then updating as admin. The comment entity should reflect the update and audit changes.

dependencies.purpose: Admin creates a post to serve as the update target.
A seller creates a comment on the post, which will be updated by the administrator.

scenario.draft: Test that when an administrator attempts to update a comment on a post but provides invalid or incomplete update data (e.g., missing body, non-boolean is_private), the API responds with a validation error and does not update the record.

dependencies.purpose: Administrator creates a post needed for comment context.
Admin creates a comment on the post to test updating it with invalid data.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a specific audit log entry by its unique identifier as an administrator. First, ensure an audit log entry exists (typically generated through an admin action, such as updating a dashboard or changing a user role). Use a valid auditLogId and administrator credentials to request its details. Confirm that the detailed audit log record is returned and matches the expected structure. Key validations: correct actor, event type, event target, creation time, and no sensitive data breach. This scenario ensures admins can access audit trail details for compliance and operational transparency.

dependencies.purpose: Generate an admin action that creates an audit log entry (e.g., create a dashboard). This supplies a valid auditLogId for use in retrieval.

scenario.draft: Verify that attempting to retrieve an audit log entry with a non-existent auditLogId results in a clear error response. This tests the system's handling of invalid UUIDs and confirms that no unauthorized or misleading information is returned. The response should clearly indicate that the requested log does not exist.

Test unauthorized access by simulating a retrieval attempt using a valid (existent) auditLogId but with a non-administrator role (e.g., customer or seller account). The request should be denied with a 'forbidden' or appropriate error, ensuring audit log privacy and role-based access control.

dependencies.purpose: Generate an audit log and obtain a valid auditLogId for the access-denied attempt.

scenario.draft: As a super administrator or a user with required permissions, attempt to delete a specific audit log entry using a valid auditLogId. Ensure an audit log row exists first (via a prior admin action). Confirm that the deletion is successful, the response returns no content, and the audit log entry is fully removed from subsequent retrieval attempts. Verify that all deletion actions are themselves logged in the audit system or that deletion cannot be reversed.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin dashboard to trigger and identify a fresh audit log entry, providing a valid auditLogId for deletion.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete an audit log using an auditLogId that does not exist. Confirm that the endpoint returns a standard not-found or error response, and no records are altered. This validates error handling for invalid UUID deletion attempts.

Simulate an attempt to delete an audit log entry using a valid auditLogId from a non-admin context (e.g., regular customer or seller role). Confirm that the request is denied with an appropriate error, preventing unauthorized log deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Generate a log entry for a valid auditLogId. Use another role's credentials to attempt the deletion.

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated administrator can successfully retrieve a paginated list of all sellers from the platform. Ensure the returned information includes all required seller fields per the schema, and that the list is paginated if necessary. Consider scenarios with both a small and a very large number of sellers to test pagination, and validate result format matches the API's contract.

dependencies.purpose: Create several seller accounts to ensure that the GET /sellers endpoint will have data to return. These sellers will be used as test data for the retrieval operation. This must be done before running the list operation.

scenario.draft: Attempt to access the GET /aimall-backend/administrator/sellers endpoint as a non-administrator (e.g., regular customer, seller, or unauthenticated user) and verify that access is denied. The response must be a permissions error code (such as 403 Forbidden) and no seller data should be returned. This tests the platform's access control restrictions.

Test the ability of an administrator to search, filter, and paginate sellers using partial business name, status, and registration date range. Validate that the filters return only sellers matching the criteria, that sorting and pagination work as expected, and that irrelevant sellers are excluded from the result set. Check that the query parameters can be combined and that pagination information is accurate.

dependencies.purpose: Create seller accounts with distinct business names, statuses, and timestamps for controlled filtering and search scenarios.

scenario.draft: Attempt to perform a search with invalid or out-of-range filter criteria (e.g., malformed dates, status not in allowed enum, negative page numbers). Ensure the API returns validation errors and does not process the request, confirming robust input validation.

Attempt to search/filter the sellers list using the PATCH endpoint as a non-admin user (customer/seller/unauthenticated). Confirm that access is denied and a permission error is returned, with no access to sensitive seller data.

A seller with a valid account attempts to retrieve their own detailed seller profile via GET /seller/sellers/{sellerId}. The response must include all defined fields, and access should be granted. Verify correctness of the returned information and ensure only the requesting seller's own data is exposed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test seller account so that this seller can log in and access their own profile.

scenario.draft: Attempt to retrieve a seller profile using a sellerId that does not exist, or try to access another seller's profile (as a different seller). Confirm that the API returns a 404 Not Found or 403 Forbidden as appropriate, and does not leak information about other sellers.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least two seller accounts, then authenticate as one and attempt to access the other's details by sellerId.

scenario.draft: As an administrator, retrieve a specific seller's details by sellerId. Verify that all fields are present in the response, including business_name, email, contact information, status, and timestamps. Ensure that sensitive information is properly returned for admin users, and handle non-existent sellerIds with a 404 error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller account so there is data available for retrieval by sellerId.

scenario.draft: As a non-administrator (seller, customer, or unauthenticated), attempt to access the administrator GET /administrator/sellers/{sellerId} endpoint. Verify that access is denied and a suitable 403 error is returned. Ensure that no sensitive seller data is exposed to unauthorized actors.

Create a new seller account using the POST /administrator/sellers endpoint, providing all required business and contact data as per the IAimallBackendSeller.ICreate schema. Confirm the seller is created successfully and all returned fields match the request and schema. Validate creation audit logs record the event. This is the success path for merchant onboarding.

Attempt to register a new seller with an email address that already exists in the system. Ensure the API returns a conflict error (409) or relevant validation failure and the new account is not created. This tests enforcement of the system's email uniqueness constraint.

dependencies.purpose: Create an initial seller with a test email address to ensure the duplicate constraint is tripped by the second request.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a seller account without providing all required fields (such as missing business name or email). Verify that the API returns a 400 Bad Request or relevant validation error indicating which fields are missing, and the account is not created. This ensures the endpoint enforces mandatory schema input validation.

Try to access the seller creation endpoint as a non-administrator (such as a customer or unauthorized user). Confirm that the operation is rejected, a 403 Forbidden or similar error is returned, and no new seller record is created. This validates role-based access restrictions to critical endpoints.

Test successful retrieval of a child (reply) comment belonging to a given parent comment. First, create a parent comment as an authenticated customer, then create a child/reply comment under that parent. Invoke the GET endpoint using both parent (commentId) and child (childCommentId) and verify that all comment fields (body, author, timestamps, parent_id) are correctly returned and the parent-child relationship is honored. Only accessible to the author, thread participant, or administrators.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent comment as an authenticated customer to obtain a valid commentId.
Create a reply (child) comment under the parent, resulting in a valid childCommentId.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval failure when the specified child comment under a parent comment has been soft deleted. Create a parent comment and a reply, then soft-delete the reply using the proper endpoint. Attempting to fetch the deleted child comment should result in a not found error, confirming the system's audit-compliance requirement and invisible state for soft-deleted threads.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent comment to serve as the thread base.
Create a reply (child) comment to obtain the childCommentId.
Soft-delete the reply to simulate a logically deleted comment.

scenario.draft: Test that an administrator (or platform moderator) can successfully retrieve the detail of a reply (child) comment under any parent comment, regardless of thread privacy, for investigation or moderation. After creating both a parent and a reply (child), call the endpoint with the admin role and verify all fields, including privacy status, are returned and correct. Access is unrestricted for admin, so even private or hidden replies are visible in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent comment for a new thread.
Create a reply (child) comment under the parent thread for use as childCommentId.

scenario.draft: Test not found error when an administrator attempts to fetch a childCommentId under a parent (commentId) where the link does not exist (i.e., the child comment exists, but is not actually a direct child of the given parent). Confirm that an appropriate error is returned, ensuring that thread integrity and hierarchical relationships are enforced. This simulates an accidental or malicious attempt to access a comment with a mismatched parent_id.

dependencies.purpose: Create two independent comments to acquire two UUIDs.
Create a reply to the first comment.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a reply (child) comment under a parent comment. As an authenticated customer, create a new parent comment, then use the POST endpoint to reply with body and privacy fields. Assert that the resulting reply comment has the correct parent_id, is_private flag set according to input, authoring customer_id, and is listed under the parent comment. This covers the main threaded reply use-case in the community system.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent comment as the thread base for replying.

scenario.draft: Test creation failure when trying to add a reply under a parent comment that is not open for replies (e.g., business logic indicates thread has been locked, is soft deleted, or restricted by settings). Attempt to reply to a soft-deleted or locked comment and expect a business error indicating that replies are not allowed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent comment.
Soft-delete the parent comment to set up locked/restricted scenario.

scenario.draft: Test validation error on trying to submit a reply (child) comment with missing or invalid required fields (such as empty body, forbidden content, missing privacy flag). The system should reject the request and return validation details, preserving data integrity.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent comment to provide a context for the reply creation.

scenario.draft: Test that the original author of a reply (child comment) can successfully update permitted fields (e.g., body, is_private) of their reply. Start by creating a parent comment and a reply, then perform an update with new field values and assert that the reply's fields have changed as expected and updated_at is properly modified.

dependencies.purpose: Create parent comment for thread context.
Create child comment (reply) under parent.

scenario.draft: Test that an attempt to update a reply (child comment) by a user who is not the original author is rejected. Set up the parent comment and reply as user A, then authenticate as user B and attempt to update the reply. The system should return an authorization error or forbidden status, confirming strict author ownership enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create the parent comment as user A.
Create the reply as user A.

scenario.draft: Test that an administrator is able to edit mutable fields (body, is_private) of any reply (child comment) in order to moderate or redact content regardless of authorship. After creating both a parent and reply, log in as admin, perform the update, and verify the server returns the edited reply with the changed content and updated_at timestamp. This confirms moderator override capability.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent comment for the thread.
Create a reply under the parent comment to be updated.

scenario.draft: Test update failure when attempting to edit a non-existent childCommentId under a parent (commentId). Provide valid parentId but an invalid or unlinked childCommentId and assert the system returns a not found (404) error, ensuring robust error reporting for administrative operations.

dependencies.purpose: Create a parent comment for testing with a valid commentId.

scenario.draft: Test successful deletion of a review attachment by the customer who owns both the review and the attachment. Steps: Register a new customer, log in, create a product and place an order, write a review, add an attachment to the review, then delete the attachment using the correct reviewId and attachmentId. Assert the attachment is no longer accessible via the detail endpoint and is absent from the review's attachments listing.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new product review by the customer to link the attachment.
Upload an attachment to the customer’s review to get a valid attachmentId for deletion.

scenario.draft: Test deletion attempt of an attachment on a review by a customer who does not own the review or the attachment. Steps: Register Customer A, create review and attachment as A, then register/log in as Customer B. Attempt to delete the attachment using A’s reviewId and attachmentId. Verify the operation is forbidden and the attachment remains intact.

dependencies.purpose: Customer A creates a review for attachment linkage.
Customer A adds an attachment to their review.

scenario.draft: Test deletion attempt with non-existent reviewId or attachmentId. Prepare a valid review, but supply a random (non-existent) attachmentId or reviewId. Confirm the API returns a not-found error and does not affect existing attachments.

dependencies.purpose: Create a review to establish a valid reviewId context before attempting invalid deletion.

scenario.draft: Test successful deletion by an administrator of any attachment on any review. Steps: Create a customer review with an attachment, then as an administrator, delete the attachment using the API. Assert that the attachment is deleted regardless of customer ownership and is gone from all listings.

dependencies.purpose: Customer creates a review to allow attachment creation.
Customer uploads an attachment to the review.
Admin deletes the attachment, validating cross-role deletion authority.

scenario.draft: Test that a seller who owns the reviewed product can delete an attachment from a review related to their product. Steps: Register a seller, create a product, customer orders/reviews and adds attachment, seller deletes the attachment. Assert the attachment is removed from the review's attachments listing.

dependencies.purpose: Seller creates a product for which the customer can later review.
Customer submits a review for the seller's product to enable attachment creation.
Customer attaches a media file to the review.

scenario.draft: Verify that a seller cannot delete attachments on reviews for products they do not own. Steps: Seller A creates Product A; Customer reviews and attaches a file to Product A. Seller B (not owner of Product A) attempts to delete the attachment from the review. Verify the API returns forbidden.

dependencies.purpose: Seller A creates Product A.
Customer reviews Seller A's product.
Customer attaches file to review.

scenario.draft: Test that attempting to delete a review attachment with an invalid or non-existent reviewId or attachmentId as a seller returns a not-found error.

dependencies.purpose: Seller creates a product to acquire a valid productId, provides context for review (even though IDs tested will be fake).

scenario.draft: Test scenario where an admin successfully deletes any attachment on any review, regardless of ownership or product association. Steps: Customer creates a review and attaches a file. Admin deletes the attachment by the API and confirms its removal from further queries.

dependencies.purpose: Customer submits a review.
Customer uploads an attachment to review.

scenario.draft: Test admin attempt to delete a review attachment using invalid reviewId or attachmentId. Steps: Use random UUIDs not corresponding to existing records and confirm not-found response.

Test successfully deleting a shipment record for an existing order as an administrator. Create an order as a prerequisite, add a shipment to that order via the shipment creation endpoint, and then delete the shipment using its shipmentId. Verify that the shipment is removed from the system and subsequent retrieval attempts return a not found error. Ensure compliance and audit trail requirements are met as described in business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new order so a shipment can be attached for deletion validation.
Add a shipment event to the previously created order and extract shipmentId for deletion.

scenario.draft: Test deletion of a shipment using a shipmentId that does not exist for a given order as an administrator. Create a valid order and try deleting with a random invalid shipmentId. Verify that the API returns an appropriate not found error and that no unintended data is deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid order as the parent for the faulty shipment deletion test.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of all audit snapshots for a specific order as a customer. Prepare a complete order as the customer, perform a few order update actions (such as status changes or item modifications) that create distinct orderSnapshot records, and then retrieve the list using the GET orderSnapshots endpoint. Validate that each snapshot reflects order state at different points in time. Ensure only snapshots for the customer's own orders are accessible.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order as the acting customer, which is required for generating snapshots.
Create at least one manual snapshot for the order; optionally trigger more via order updates.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of order snapshots for an order where no snapshots have ever been created. Create a new order as a customer and immediately attempt to list snapshots. Confirm that the API returns an empty array or page and does not error. This validates correct handling of edge case with no history records.

dependencies.purpose: Provision an order as the customer to be used for snapshot retrieval; do not create any snapshots.

scenario.draft: Test that a seller can retrieve all audit snapshots for an order they manage. Create an order as the seller, apply several updates or trigger state changes to produce multiple order snapshot records, and then fetch the full list as the seller. Confirm only relevant snapshots (for their orders) are returned and privacy boundaries of other sellers are maintained.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order as the seller; orderId will be used for downstream operations.
Create manual and/or automatic order snapshots for history validation.

scenario.draft: Test that a seller is prohibited from retrieving order snapshots for an order they do not own. Create two orders—one for each of two different sellers. Attempt to fetch the orderSnapshots for the other seller's order. Expect the API to return an authorization error, validating business logic and access control enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Create orders for two different sellers to set up the cross-access scenario.

scenario.draft: Test that an administrator can retrieve all audit snapshots for any given order, regardless of customer or seller. Generate multiple snapshots for an order across its lifecycle, then retrieve them using the administrator endpoint. Confirm that the admin receives all existing snapshot records and that the data matches the order's historic changes.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order for full administrative access and manipulation.
Create multiple order snapshot history records via updates and direct post operations.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving order snapshots for a non-existent orderId as administrator. Try to fetch orderSnapshots for a random or deleted order. Confirm the API returns a not found error and does not leak data or system information.

Test searching order snapshots for a customer's order using filter and pagination options. Create an order and generate snapshots with different event types or timestamps. Use the PATCH endpoint with filters for date range or event type and verify that the returned set matches the filters. Validate that the pagination works correctly and only snapshots for the customer's own order are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create the order as customer, to be used for generating and filtering order snapshots.
Create at least a few varying order snapshot records (by type/time) for filtering.

scenario.draft: Test searching order snapshots for an order with invalid filter criteria as a customer. Create an order and attempt to search with filters that result in no matches (such as a non-existent event type or an out-of-range date). Confirm that the API returns an empty result set. Also, try malformed filter input and validate that appropriate validation or error responses are returned and no sensitive data is leaked.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order for the customer; needed as base for search tests.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a new abuse incident by an administrator with valid event type and all required context fields. Ensure that a new incident record can be created successfully, that required audit fields are populated, and that it appears in subsequent incident listings. Validate that detection time and type match input, and that the record is initially unresolved.

Test the failure of creating an abuse incident with missing required fields (such as omitting the event type or context). Attempt the POST operation as an admin and verify the API responds with a validation error detailing missing fields, and that no incident is created.

Simulate creation of two abuse incidents with identical type and context fields in rapid succession. Validate whether system deduplication or business logic prevents duplicate incident logging, or if both records are stored. Confirm expected business behavior for repeated incident triggers.

Test updating an existing abuse incident's resolved status from unresolved to resolved by an administrator. Ensure that only allowed fields change, audit logging is performed, and the resolved status/time are updated. Confirm that inappropriate field mutation (such as changing detected_at or context) is rejected.

dependencies.purpose: Create an abuse incident record to obtain an abuseIncidentId for update testing.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update immutable or restricted fields (e.g., detected_at or primary context fields) on an abuse incident using PUT. Verify that the API rejects the update with a proper validation error, leaving existing values unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Generate a valid abuse incident for update attempts.

scenario.draft: Test hard deletion of an abuse incident by an administrator. After deleting, confirm the record is fully removed from incident listings and detail endpoints, and that an audit log (if required by policy) is created for this destructive action. Attempt to access the removed incident to verify it returns not found.

dependencies.purpose: Create an abuse incident for later deletion.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete an abuse incident using a non-existent or already-deleted abuseIncidentId. Confirm that the API responds with a 404 not found or appropriate error code for invalid deletion attempts, and no other records are affected.

As an authenticated customer, retrieve the list of support tickets for your own account, where multiple tickets exist with different statuses (open, resolved). Validate that only tickets belonging to the current customer are returned and that all relevant fields (subject, status, priority, timestamps) are present.

dependencies.purpose: Create several support tickets for the test customer to populate the listing.

scenario.draft: As an authenticated customer, fetch the support ticket list when no tickets have been created yet. Validate that the API returns an empty array or result set and does not expose ticket records belonging to other users.

As a seller, retrieve the list of support tickets you have opened. Validate the API only returns tickets where the current seller is the requester, not those belonging to unrelated customers or sellers. Confirm support for multiple ticket categories or priorities for the seller role.

dependencies.purpose: Create support tickets as a seller for proper test coverage.

scenario.draft: Ensure that when a seller has not opened any support tickets, the GET operation returns an empty list and does not leak tickets from other roles.

Simulate a seller attempting to access support tickets for a different customer or unrelated account. Confirm that only their own tickets are retrievable through this endpoint, reinforcing role-based access controls.

dependencies.purpose: Create support tickets for a customer to ensure they exist for the negative test scenario.

scenario.draft: Verify that an administrator can retrieve all attachments for a specific community post by providing a valid postId. First, create a test post with at least one attachment as the administrator or another permitted role. Then, use the administrator context to call the GET /aimall-backend/administrator/posts/{postId}/attachments endpoint. Check that the attachments returned match what was uploaded, all required metadata fields (file_uri, type, size, etc) are present, and the pagination (if applicable) is correct.

dependencies.purpose: Create a community post as a prerequisite for having a postId.
Upload one or more attachments to associate with the created post.

scenario.draft: Ensure the API returns an appropriate error when an administrator attempts to retrieve attachments for a postId that does not exist. Attempt to call the GET /aimall-backend/administrator/posts/{postId}/attachments endpoint with a random, non-existent UUID. Confirm the API responds with a 404 or suitable error indication.

Verify the endpoint returns an empty result set when retrieving attachments for a valid post that has no attachments. Create a post as the administrator but do not upload any attachments. scenario.draft: Try updating a cart using a non-existent or invalid cartId as admin. Verify the system responds with a not found or validation error and does not create or update any cart data.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a shopping cart using a non-existent or invalid cartId. The system should return a not found or validation error and not perform any deletion.

Test successful creation of a new analytics dashboard configuration by an administrator. Validate that the system enforces uniqueness of the dashboard code, and that upon success, the created dashboard is returned with all expected fields populated. This scenario confirms compliance with business policy that only administrators can create dashboards.

Test failure case when attempting to create a new analytics dashboard configuration using a dashboard code that already exists in the system. First, create a dashboard with a specific code. Then, attempt to create a second dashboard using the same code. The API should reject the duplicate with a clear violation error, enforcing uniqueness constraints.

scenario.draft: Test failure scenario where the administrator attempts to create a new analytics dashboard but omits one or more required fields (e.g., missing title or config JSON). The API should return validation errors indicating precisely which required fields are missing, and creation should be blocked.

Test rejection when a non-administrator or unauthorized user attempts to create a new analytics dashboard configuration. The system must deny the request with an appropriate authorization error, ensuring only designated administrators are permitted to perform this action.

Test successful update of an existing analytics dashboard configuration. The administrator provides a valid dashboard ID and a set of updatable fields (e.g., title, description, config JSON). Ensure the system applies the changes, returns the updated dashboard record, and validates any uniqueness constraints as necessary.

scenario.draft: Test the system's behavior when attempting to update a dashboard's code to a value that is already in use by another dashboard. First, create two dashboards with different codes, then attempt to update the second one's code to match the first. The operation should fail with a uniqueness constraint violation.

dependencies.purpose: Create two dashboards with distinct codes to set up for the duplicate code update test.

scenario.draft: Test rejection when updating an analytics dashboard with an incomplete request lacking required updatable fields (such as missing a new title when title is mandatory in update). The API should return detailed validation errors and must not modify the dashboard.
